🕳️🛠️ **F-2672-2 — CAUSED AND CAUGHT INSIDE THE SAME FIRE (s2672, 2026-09-24): ADDING AN IMPORT TO A SCRIPT THAT MUTATION HARNESSES COPY *OUT OF ITS DIRECTORY* BREAKS EVERY MUTATION ARM AT ONCE — AND THE BREAKAGE WEARS THE COSTUME OF THE ARMS WORKING.** Three guard files (`ledger-mirror-exposure-guard`, `ledger-mirror-column-class-guard`, and the freshness guard's fixture) manufacture their defects by writing an EDITED COPY of the subject into a temp directory and running it there. When this fire gave `scripts/ledger-mirror-exposure.mjs` a relative import of the new shared resolver (`./ledger-mirror-dest.mjs`, F-2668-2's cure), every such copy lost its import and died on `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before executing a line. **10 of 1,241 arms red in the battery**, all of them MANUFACTURED arms — i.e. the arms whose entire job is to fail — plus one arm asserting a property the re-home deliberately retired. 🎯 **THE HAZARD IS THE COSTUME, not the crash: a variant that cannot LOAD produces a non-zero exit and no output, which is indistinguishable at a glance from a variant the guard correctly refused.** In a harness without a control-validity check, all four column-class arms and all five exposure arms would have gone GREEN — each one "catching" a mutation it never ran. ✅ **WHAT SAVED IT WAS A PREDECESSOR'S SCAR, and that is the whole argument for the check:** both harnesses carry `runVariant`'s assertion that *"the variant produced NO stdout ... it did not run, so this arm proves nothing"*, written after F-2215-1 when every variant arm in the sibling guard passed VACUOUSLY on first writing (macOS `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` defeated the module-main check). That assertion converted a silent nine-arm false green into a loud red with the reason printed. ⚖️ **SEVERITY, HONESTLY: REALISED COST ZERO** — the battery runs BEFORE the clearing commit by F-E1T-2's order, so the red was seen, diagnosed and cured in the same fire and nothing shipped; the repair is three lines (`cpSync` the resolver beside each variant) and the six ledger-mirror guard files read **74/74, rc 0** after it. 💡 **REUSABLE: when you add an import to a script, ask who COPIES that script somewhere else.** Mutation harnesses, scratch-worktree gates and relocation fixtures all move a subject away from its siblings, and a relative import is the one thing that does not survive the trip. **How to apply: `grep -rn "writeFileSync(file\|cpSync(SUBJECT\|copyFileSync(SUBJECT" scripts/*.test.mjs` before adding a relative import to any guarded script, and never let a harness treat "the variant produced nothing" as a pass.** GATE: none — cured in the same commit; the three harnesses now carry the resolver and the control-validity assertions that caught it are untouched.
🕳️🛠️ **F-2672-1 — CURED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE GATE IT GUARDS (s2672 fire 2026-09-24, filed while closing F-2668-2): A CURE'S OWN INSTRUCTIONS FOR ITS FUTURE MAINTENANCE CAN CARRY THE EXACT DEFECT THE CURE EXISTS TO PREVENT — AND THEY ARE READ AT THE ONE MOMENT NOBODY RE-DERIVES THEM.** `ops/ledger-series-anchor.json` is F-2671-1's cure: the LB-01 freshness guard's denominator, deliberately placed OUTSIDE the directory it audits so that losing the mirrors cannot also lose the record of how many there should have been. Its `whenToEditThis` field told the next fire, in writing: *"Only when LB-01's destination is RE-HOMED … **Move the day forward in the SAME commit as the re-home** and record why here."* I am that next fire, and the re-home is exactly what I did. **FOLLOWING THAT INSTRUCTION WOULD HAVE MOVED `firstCoverageDay` FROM 2026-08-24 TO 2026-09-24 AND DELETED 31 DAYS OF COVERAGE FROM THE DENOMINATOR** — leaving the guard to print `1/1 day(s) present`, `✅ WHOLE AND CURRENT`, `rc 0` over a series whose old end had just been moved somewhere it no longer looked. That is F-2671-1's false green, character for character, re-manufactured by obeying F-2671-1's own cure. ⚖️ **SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: REALISED COST ZERO.** The instruction was never executed — the day stayed 2026-08-24 and the live guard reads `32/32, 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-24, rc 0` at the new home, with every file re-hashed across the move. The row exists for the CLASS, not for a wound. 🔍 **WHY THE INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG, precisely, because "be careful" is not a cure:** it silently assumed a re-home is a DISCONTINUITY — a new destination starting an empty series. A re-home is a MOVE. All 32 files were renamed across and re-hashed at the destination against their pre-move digests (32/32 equal, `artifacts/s2672/rehome-mirrors.txt`), so the series never restarted and its first covered day never changed. The author conflated *"the directory changed"* with *"the coverage changed"*, and only the second is what the anchor declares. 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a new axis beside [[a-span-guard-calls-a-lost-series-whole]]: an external denominator is only as good as the RULE FOR UPDATING IT, and that rule is consumed at exactly the moment its author is not there to re-derive it.** A maintenance instruction is CODE WITH NO TEST AND NO READER-CHECK: nothing executes it, nothing reds when it is wrong, and it is obeyed under time pressure by the one person doing the very migration it describes. **How to apply: when you write "edit this file when X happens", write the PREDICATE that makes the edit correct, not the EVENT that prompts it** — here, "edit it when the series' first covered DAY changes; a move that carries every file across is not such a change" — and where you can, make the wrong edit red a guard rather than a reader. 🔧 **CURED IN THE SAME COMMIT:** `whenToEditThis` now states the predicate, names this non-change as its worked example, and the `history` array carries the re-home as a deliberate UNCHANGED entry, so the next reader can see the question was asked and answered rather than skipped. GATE: none — the instruction is rewritten and arm 21 still asserts the repo ships a readable, non-future anchor.
🕳️🛠️ **F-2671-2 — CURED s2673 `12ccef83a` (filed s2671 2026-09-24, MEASURED BY CAUSING IT — and keyed 🕳️, NOT the desk glyph, because this is a factory finding and not an item awaiting the owner): TAKING THE LOCK WITH `status-line1.mjs set` DISPLACES THE PREDECESSOR'S HANDOFF LINE — AND WITH IT THE ONLY CURRENT COPY OF THE OWNER'S-DESK TAIL — INTO GIT AND NOWHERE ELSE, FOR THE WHOLE LENGTH OF THE FIRE.** This is documented behaviour, not a tool defect: `scripts/status-line1.mjs:43-48` says plainly that `set` does not archive, that the line your handoff then archives is your OWN lock line, and that a predecessor's unarchived handoff must be recovered with `git show <their-commit>:STATUS.md`. I read that file for its `{STAMP}` contract, used `set`, and dropped s2670's 7,974-char handoff line — including its verbatim desk tail, the header and all three items — out of STATUS at 20:26:30 local; restored 11 minutes later at 20:37:08 from `452e79707` (`ff1d6ee59`) — both times read from `git log --format=%ci`, after the first draft of this row GUESSED "about 25 minutes" and the command corrected it, which is the same reflex this repo already outlawed for STATUS stamps. **STATED AT ITS REAL SIZE AND NOT INFLATED:** the items also live in `docs/OWNER-DESK-2026-09-19.md` and in every older archived handoff bullet, so nothing was unrecoverable and the count never moved from three. What the gap costs is that STATUS's newest desk copy silently ages by one fire, and a fire that DIES between its lock and its handoff — the F-E1T-2 shape, which has happened here — leaves the current desk in git alone while every STATUS reader sees the predecessor's. The desk is the one surface whose whole purpose is to be read by the owner without a git command. **CURE, a habit rather than a patch:** write the handoff with `node scripts/status-line1.mjs handoff <textfile> "sNNNN lock"`, which archives the displaced line by construction, and a fire that took the lock with `set` owes a check that the PREDECESSOR's handoff bullet exists before it clears. GATE: either `status-line1.mjs set` refuses, or warns loudly, when the line it is about to displace carries the desk tail and no matching archive bullet exists — or this row is accepted as habit-only and says so. NOT CURED HERE, deliberately: the fix belongs in the tool every fire reads, and the instrument that would score exactly this (`scripts/status-archive-audit.mjs`) still cannot run on a 20.5 MB STATUS.md — it burned nine minutes at 3.5% CPU for s2670 and produced no verdict, UNVERIFIED there and not re-run here. ✅ **GATE ANSWERED s2673, the first of the two branches it offered rather than the habit-only one:** `status-line1.mjs set` now REFUSES when all three hold — the displaced line carries a desk tail, the new line does not carry it forward intact, and no archive bullet below already holds the displaced line. Any one of those failing means nothing is lost, so the refusal cannot fire on lawful work: carrying the tail onto the lock line never sees it, and `handoff` preserves by construction and is not checked at all. `--allow-desk-drop` covers the one lawful shape the predicate cannot see (a ruled item leaving the tail, fire.md §4) and WARNS rather than going quiet. Both printed remedies ADD words and neither removes any, because this repo has twice been bitten by a guard whose remedy was to corrupt a correct file (`status-archive-audit.mjs:322`, F-2088-2). TEETH: `scripts/status-line1-desk-displacement-guard.test.mjs`, 10 arms / 10 pass, registered in `test:ledger-guards`; arm 1 asserts the CONTROL is valid before arms 2-3 are believed (F-2215-1 — the pre-cure subject accepts the drop and the desk leaves the fixture board), arm 3 asserts the refusal is ATOMIC, and arms 4-7 + 10 are the lawful shapes that must keep passing. Measured against the real 20.5 MB board in a copy (`artifacts/s2673/live-board-probe.mjs`): desk-less `set` rc 1 naming F-2671-2 with the board byte-identical, the same `set` carrying the tail rc 0 with all three items intact. 🔍 **AND THE ROW'S OWN BLOCKER WAS FALSE — see F-2673-1:** `status-archive-audit.mjs` was never unable to run. Its battery leg answers this board in **5.8 s**. What cost s2670 nine minutes was the BARE invocation walking all 5,857 STATUS.md commits, priced here at 9.7 min; it was working, not hung, and was killed at roughly its own finishing time. This fire's archive chain was scored by the instrument, not structurally: CLEAN, 0 permanently absent.

🔢 **F-2670-1 (s2670 fire 2026-09-24, measured while discharging F-2668-2): "NO LOCAL REF OF 12,965 CARRIES THE PATH" IS A TRUE SENTENCE OVER A POPULATION THAT IS 99.8% GRAFTS AND CONTAINS NOT ONE REF FROM THE REMOTE IT WAS ANSWERING ABOUT.** s2668 disproved a claim about the PRIVATE ARCHIVE by searching this repo's refs and quoting their count. Counted this fire with `git for-each-ref`: **`refs/replace/*` 12,937** (the flat-git grafts of F-2665-1), `refs/heads/*` 15, `refs/tags/*` 11, `refs/remotes/*` **2** — and both of those are `origin/HEAD` and `origin/main`. **`refs/remotes/archive/*` = 0.** So the real searchable population behind the imposing 12,965 was **28 refs**, and every one of the archive's **611** heads lay outside it by construction: the repo has never fetched that remote, so no search of it could ever find anything there, and a null result was guaranteed before the question was asked. The number did the persuading precisely because it was large. **Why it is a class, not a slip:** a graft namespace inflates a ref count by three orders of magnitude while contributing nothing searchable, and remote-tracking coverage is invisible in the total — both of which make "I searched N refs" read as thorough exactly when it is empty. **How to apply:** before a ref count is used as a denominator, subtract `refs/replace/*` and name WHICH REMOTES are represented in what remains; a question about remote R is answerable only over refs that came from R, so the cheap prior check is `git for-each-ref refs/remotes/R` (zero means ask `git ls-remote R` or a temp-dir clone instead, never the local ref table). Sibling: [[a-span-guard-calls-a-lost-series-whole]] — the same shape, a denominator taken from inside the thing being audited. Evidence: `artifacts/s2670/archive-ledger-probe.txt` (557 heads fetched and searched, against the 28 that were reachable before).

⚡ **F-2665-1 — THE FLAT GIT COST IS 12,937 REPLACE REFS, NOT THE MISSING COMMIT-GRAPH: s2664's HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY DIRECT EXPERIMENT, ITS MAGNITUDE IS ~2.3× OVER, AND THE REAL CURE IS 20× (measured s2665).** s2664 measured a flat per-invocation git cost, correctly labelled the commit-graph link an INFERENCE, and handed it forward as priority (C): *"RUN IT ON A QUIET BOARD AND RE-MEASURE."* I ran it. `git commit-graph write --reachable` took **371 ms** and produced a 780 KB cache — and **NOTHING MOVED**: `rev-list --count main` `534 → 463 ms`, `merge-base --is-ancestor` `494 → 512`, `rev-list --count --max-count=1` `413 → 410`, all within noise, one arm SLOWER. 🔬 **THEN I ISOLATED IT, and the tell was available for free the whole time: `rev-parse HEAD` (resolves a ref, never opens the object store) is `14 ms`, while `cat-file -t HEAD` — which reads exactly ONE object — is `348 ms`. No commit-graph story can explain that, because `rev-parse` walks no graph either. The toll is paid at OBJECT-STORE INITIALIZATION, before any traversal begins.** 📊 **CAUSE, MEASURED: the repo carries `12,956` refs of which **`12,937` are `refs/replace/*`** left by the A3 rewrite, stored as **`12,945` LOOSE ref files** against a `1,096`-byte `packed-refs`. Replace refs ALTER OBJECT RESOLUTION, so git must load every one before it can look up a single object — which is why the cost is flat, per-invocation, and indifferent to how much you walk.** ✅ **CURE: `git pack-refs --all` — `4,914 ms`, once. PAYOFF MEASURED AT THE SAME LOAD (16.27 against 16.38/16.76 before, so the conditions are matched rather than hoped for — F-2452-1): `cat-file -t HEAD` `348 → 17 ms` (**20×**) · `log -1` `337 → 16` (**21×**) · `rev-list --count --max-count=1` `413 → 18` (**23×**) · `for-each-ref` `301 → 19` (**16×**) · `rev-list --count main` `534 → 106` (**5.0×**) · `merge-base --is-ancestor` `494 → 104` (**4.8×**) · `git status --porcelain` `492 → 100` (**4.9×**).** 🔒 **NON-DESTRUCTIVE AND PROVEN SO RATHER THAN ASSERTED: `pack-refs` changes ref STORAGE, never ref CONTENT. I banked the complete `name → objectname → objecttype` map for all 12,956 refs BEFORE (`artifacts/s2665/refmap-before.txt`, control-asserted non-trivial at >12,000 rows), re-took it after, and compared ref-for-ref: **`0` LOST, `0` MOVED, `0` ADDED — 12,956 identical both sides.** The live lane-c Astra runner (pid 44705) was ALIVE across the operation and unharmed.** ⛔ **AND THE REPLACE REFS ARE LOAD-BEARING — DO NOT EVER "TIDY" THEM AWAY, which is the destructive act this finding could otherwise invite: they are the map from PRE-rewrite hashes to live commits, verified rather than assumed (`0007011aa04e → 0428e85b1c6b`, and `cat-file -t` on the OLD id returns `commit`). They are what keeps this factory's enormous body of historical hash citations resolvable. `pack-refs` PRESERVES all 12,937; deletion would silently break every pre-A3 citation at once.** ⓘ **The map covers SURVIVORS only, and the law already knows it: `9ec7c4037`, `220fbe472` and `b9e21bacf` genuinely do NOT resolve — those paths were dropped by the A3 shrink, which is exactly why the ledger annotates them *"(archive: pruned by the A3 rewrite)"*.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, NOT a false green, nothing was broken and NO VERDICT ANYWHERE WAS WRONG — every instrument returned the right answer, merely slowly. What earns it a row is that s2664 published this factory-wide (*"this silently re-prices every graph-walking instrument"*) and named a cure that does not work, so the next fire would have spent its budget on a 371 ms no-op and concluded the cost was irreducible.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is measured rather than lazy: loose refs accumulate LAWFULLY (every fetch, every branch, every rewrite writes them), so a red on "refs are loose" would fire during ordinary correct operation and be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). `git gc --auto` packs them on its own schedule; what was missing was a reader who knew to look. The cure is this row plus the corrected clause at the site.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is F-2480-1's shape on a new subject: that finding was ARITHMETICALLY RIGHT AND CAUSALLY WRONG; so was this one, with the magnitude ~2.3× over on top (s2664's `~1.2 s` does not reproduce — I measure `0.41`–`0.57 s` at HIGHER load, which is F-2620-2's lesson that adjacent runs measure one moment's conditions). **When a flat per-invocation cost is blamed on a TRAVERSAL cache, test a command that touches exactly ONE object. If it pays the same toll, the cost is at INITIALIZATION and the cache is the wrong subject entirely.** The hypothesis was honestly labelled and honestly handed forward — and the only thing that separated the true cause from the plausible one was running the experiment the predecessor asked for.**

🧪 **F-2665-2 — THE COMMIT-GRAPH IS NOW PRESENT AND BUYS NOTHING MEASURABLE; DO NOT RE-TAKE THIS EXPERIMENT (a NEGATIVE banked with its mechanism, F-2214-1).** I wrote it (371 ms, 780 KB at `.git/objects/info/commit-graph`) and it is LEFT IN PLACE — it is a standard derived cache that `git gc --auto` writes on its own schedule, it costs 780 KB, and removing it would be a second unmeasured change. **But it is credited with NONE of F-2665-1's speedup**, and that was established TWICE rather than argued: once with refs still loose (every probe unchanged within noise), and again AFTER packing, by toggling `-c core.commitGraph=true|false` — a read-only A/B that needs no deletion — across interleaved runs: `rev-list --count main` `89` vs `94 ms`, `merge-base --is-ancestor` `90` vs `116`, `log -1` `18` vs `18`, and `rev-list --all --count` `116` vs `98`, i.e. **SLOWER with the graph**. Deltas are ±25 ms in both directions on a 12,994-commit repo: noise. ⓘ **So if a future fire finds git slow here, the subject is REF STORAGE (F-2665-1), never the graph — and `-c core.commitGraph=false` is the cheap way to re-check that without touching the cache.**

On the conditions that ACTUALLY OBTAIN on this machine today, this leg sits at `84–95%` of its bound and tips over at load `~30`, so the "re-run it alone" remedy costs a fire ~200 s every time the board is busy, and will eventually stop working.** 🚫 **DELIBERATELY NOT EXECUTED, AND THE RESTRAINT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN TIMID: raising a bound to make a red go away is F-1410-2 in its named costume, and I cannot tell a thin margin from a slow machine without a TRUE QUIET BASELINE, which I could not take — the lane-c Astra run and the A3 archive work held this machine at load `18–30` for my entire fire. What it does not give is a MARGIN — and a discriminator that keeps returning "contention, ignore it" is indistinguishable from one whose subject is quietly approaching its ceiling. **When you dismiss a red as contention, record how much of the bound the GREEN run consumed; the verdict is in the exit code, but the warning is in the headroom.**

What no digest has is any reason to believe that denominator is the DAY.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is the DIRECTION and the ABSENCE OF ANY INSTRUMENT: a digest is the owner's one-morning-action account of a day, so a player-visible land missing from it is news the owner never sees — and unlike the gazette, which has a sweep that re-offers a candidate until it is judged, **NOTHING audits a digest for completeness at all**. F-2623-1 also prices the permanent half: a commit that leaves the first-parent walk can never be offered again, so on a day that DID orphan one, both the sweep and the digest would miss it and neither would say so.** ➡️ **THEREFORE, WHEN COMPILING A TK-01 DIGEST: take the day's set from ALL commits reachable from HEAD carrying that `%cs`, not from `--first-parent` alone, and for every off-walk player-path commit test CONTAINMENT before concluding anything. An off-walk commit contained in a walk commit is ordinary branch-side history and is accounted for; one contained in nothing is an orphan and is the day's missing news. Both counts belong in the digest's method note — they now stand in `marketing/outbox/ticker-digest-2026-09-19.md`.** ⚠️ **DO NOT read this fire's `0 orphaned` as licence to skip the check — read it as the check being cheap (two `git log` walks) and this day being lucky. The risk is real and unrealised, which is the state in which a check is easiest to drop.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: *"is this digest complete?"* is a judgement over prose, and the only mechanical key — *"reachable != first-parent on this day"* — is TRUE on essentially every day that carries a merge, so a red would fire during ordinary correct operation and be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). It is the same restraint F-2391-1, F-2562-2 and F-2598-1 all took for this very duty. The cure is the sentence you are reading, plus the method note now standing in the digest itself.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is F-2634-1's lesson landing on a DUTY instead of a TOOL: that finding showed a reading instruction written for one instrument silently fails to cover the sibling the same paragraph prescribes. Here F-2623-1 correctly established the re-rooting hazard FOR THE GAZETTE SWEEP — and the TK-01 digest reads the SAME corpus, by the SAME walk, for a DIFFERENT consumer, and nobody carried it across. **When you find a hazard in how an instrument selects its subject set, enumerate every OTHER duty that selects the same way** — the sweep and the digest differ only in who reads the answer, and only one of them was ever warned.** ⓘ **A NOTE ON ITS OWN LANDING, because it is the kind of thing this ledger exists to keep: this row was DEFERRED at first. When I went to write it, `tasks/BACKLOG.md` was carrying an attended session's UNCOMMITTED owner rulings (A14, F-ASTRA-2, A3) — four files written in the same second — and a path-scoped `git add` stages the WHOLE FILE, so committing the row would have swept those rulings into a fire's commit under a fire's message (the F-1589-5 attribution class). This shows it records nothing about its CLOCK either — a filename carries a date and never the convention that produced it, so the bucketing rule is invisible in the artifact and recoverable ONLY from the commits it cites. 🔎 **F-2619-1 — A CANDIDATE'S COMMIT DATE IS ITS *CREATION* TIME, NOT ITS *ARRIVAL* ON MAIN, SO IT CANNOT TELL YOU WHETHER YOUR PREDECESSOR SHOULD HAVE SEEN IT (measured s2619).** The GZ-01 sweep returned `6` candidates — the first non-zero set in eight fires — and THREE of them carry `%cI` timestamps that PREDATE the previous fire's lock: `1c47ba975` `08:36:33`, `220fbe472 (archive: pruned by the A3 rewrite)` `08:45:13` and `1d05615c6` `08:46:02`, against s2618's lock commit `f89cf5ef8` at `08:55:45`. Read as arrival times they say s2618 swept a board already holding two player-visible drains and published `candidates 0` — i.e. that a correct predecessor walked past the exact thing this duty exists to catch. 📊 **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, and the inference I nearly published was wrong: main's tip at s2618's lock was its first parent `133f80804` (s2617's handoff, `07:49:02`), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1c47ba975 f89cf5ef8` answers NO. Every one of the three was created in an ATTENDED WORKTREE on a branch and entered main's first-parent chain later, when `d853af7cc` landed at `09:31`. s2618's `candidates 0` was TRUE, and so was s2617's.** ⚠️ **I TRIED AND REFUTED AN ARITHMETIC SHORTCUT FIRST, which is why this row exists rather than an accusation: the `examined` counts differ by `5903 − 5884 = 19`, and `1c47ba975` sits at first-parent index `19`, so the two numbers appear to prove main's tip WAS that commit — off by exactly one from the truth. A ±1 coincidence in a 5,900-commit corpus reads as a proof; the ancestry question is decidable in one command and needs no arithmetic at all.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, nothing is broken, NOT a false green, and no verdict anywhere was wrong — the sweep behaved correctly at every step and every fire in the chain reported truthfully.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is the DIRECTION: it fails toward a FALSE ACCUSATION against a predecessor that did its duty, and toward distrusting the one instrument that catches attended bursts (F-1546-1 keys GZ-01 on the MERGE EVENT, not on who drained, so an attended burst lands a judgement duty on whichever fire holds the lock next — this is the fourth occurrence of the pattern s2612 first flagged).** ➡️ **THEREFORE: to ask whether a predecessor should have seen a candidate, ask ANCESTRY against that fire's own lock commit — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <candidate> <their lock>` — never the candidate's `%cI`, and never a difference of `examined` counts.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: a commit created on a branch and merged later is the ordinary, lawful shape of every attended drain, so a red on "this commit's date precedes its arrival" would fire during routine correct operation and be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate) — the same restraint F-2567-1 took for a hand-typed clock and F-2391-1 for a hand-typed window. The cure is the row you are reading.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is F-2567-1's axis turned on a different clock: that finding showed a derived AGE carries a hidden parameter (which clock you subtract from). This one shows a recorded TIMESTAMP carries a hidden parameter too — WHICH EVENT IT STAMPS. `%cI` stamps creation; the fact a fire actually needs is reachability, and the two diverge by however long a branch sits unmerged. When a timestamp is about to settle a question of who knew what when, ask what event it records before you let it answer.**

✏️ **F-2575-1 — A CONTENDED BATTERY DOES NOT ONLY MOVE A TIMING *ASSERTION*, IT BLOWS A *SPAWN BOUND* — AND A BLOWN BOUND REPORTS AS A TIMEOUT, WHICH READS AS A WEDGE AND AIMS THE NEXT FIRE AT THE WRONG SUBJECT ENTIRELY.** Measured s2575 on a dry board, under an attended load spike. ✅ **THE VERDICT FIRST: NOTHING IS BROKEN. `scripts/gazette-scan-space-guard.test.mjs` run ALONE is `rc=0, 9/9 pass` in `114.9 s`, and its slowest arm — *"the scan space is DECLARED on stdout"*, which spawns the full-history `gazette-backfill-sweep` — takes `114.6 s` of its `240_000 ms` F-2430-1 bound.** 📊 **THE MEASUREMENT, one tree, the ONLY variable being what else was running: battery run 1 (load ordinary) → that leg PASSED, `125.2 s` total; battery run 2, same tree but for a baseline re-pin, machine at **load average `99.74` on 16 CPUs** → that leg reported `✖ ... (240002.849167ms)`, i.e. the bound firing to the millisecond, `280.1 s` total; the leg re-run ALONE moments later → `rc=0`, `114.9 s`. **A 2.1× swing across the bound, against a guard whose subject I never touched.** ✅ **AND THEN THE CONTROL THAT ISOLATES THE VARIABLE, which is stronger than the re-run-alone arm because it changes only the machine: once load fell to `11.10` the WHOLE battery was re-run on that same tree and the same leg passed with no timeout (`172.8 s`, every node leg green). So "run it ALONE" is NOT the explanatory variable — CONTENTION is, and the aloneness cure works only because it happens to remove it.**** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, NOT a false green, and the bound behaved EXACTLY as F-2430-1 designed — it failed LOUD and named its subject, which is the whole point of that cure. That finding established that contention manufactures findings by moving a timing ASSERTION — a `p95` against a cap — and its cure is *"run it ALONE"*. This is the same contamination arriving through the SPAWN BOUND instead, and the two do not read alike: an assertion failure prints a number against a cap and invites you to doubt the number, while a bound failure prints `ETIMEDOUT` at exactly `240002 ms` and invites you to doubt whether anything is RUNNING. **That is the wedge signature F-2429-1 and F-2563-3 describe, so the reader is pointed at `ps`, at grandchild checks, at §2.0b — a whole diagnostic ladder built for a process that is stuck, for a leg that is merely queued behind ninety-nine other runnable threads.** The tell that separates them is the ARITHMETIC, not the stack: a bound that fires at its exact value on a leg that passes alone is CONTENTION; a wedge blows every bound in the chain and ignores SIGTERM.** 📐 **AND THE HEADROOM IS THE HALF WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, because it is F-2465-2 landing on a SECOND subject: `240_000` was applied to all 83 sites MECHANICALLY by F-2430-1, and F-2465-2 already corrected it once (`fixture-teardown`, whose child is itself a battery at `326.2 s`, i.e. ABOVE the house bound). This leg is the mirror case — `114.6 s`, **48% of its bound consumed on a quiet machine** — and its child is a FULL-HISTORY scan over `marketing/outbox/` and every first-parent commit, so **its cost grows monotonically with the repo while the bound stays fixed.** The margin is not a property of the guard; it is a race between the corpus and a constant.** 🚫 **NO CURE SHIPPED, and the restraint is measured rather than lazy. Raising the bound is F-1410-2 in its named costume (*raise it until it goes green*) and would blind the one case the bound exists for; lowering it reds honest work; and pinning a duration reds on every slower machine and is excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate) — which is exactly why F-2413-1 and F-2414-1 BOTH declined a guard for this battery’s wall time. **The cure is this row plus the sentence in `scripts/fire.md` §3.** ➡️ **THEREFORE, BINDING, AND IT COSTS ONE COMMAND: before you report a battery red as a finding, read `uptime`. At load ≈ 100 on 16 CPUs the battery is not an instrument, and BOTH its assertions and its bounds are measuring the machine. Re-run the failing leg ALONE and report what THAT says — and say plainly in the handoff that the aggregate did not come back clean, rather than reporting a green you did not get.** 💡 **REUSABLE: F-2452-1 showed a scalar COST is a measurement with a hidden parameter (load); F-2567-1 showed a derived AGE has one (the clock). **A BOUND HAS ONE TOO, AND IT IS THE SAME PARAMETER — but where a cost is merely *quoted* wrong, a bound *converts* the hidden parameter into a categorical verdict: PASS or TIMEOUT, with no number in the failure to hint that load was the variable.** When a timeout fires at exactly its configured value, treat the configured value as the thing you measured, not the subject. (s2575, 2026-09-15)

The cure is the sentence you are reading.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a NEW AXIS after *how WIDE is the selector* (F-2358-1), *can its axis EXPRESS the defect* (F-2389-1), *which TREE* (F-2484-1), *a registry is not a census* (F-2485-1), *how many subjects did the author VISIT* (F-2487-1/F-2488-1), *entries vs files* (F-2490-1), *no durability predicate* (F-2560-1) and *an undeclared denominator* (F-2561-1): all of those interrogate the SUBJECT SET or the PREDICATE. **This one interrogates the INSTRUMENT THAT CHECKS THE PREDICATE.** When a cure says content may be preserved "in another SHAPE", remember SHAPE includes the PATH — a transform that splits, relocates and re-names is free to move every coordinate except the one the manifest records on purpose.

THE REAL MECHANISM, read rather than inherited: the refusal DID reach stderr (8,783 `gr-sim rejected orders:` lines), but `gr-sim.readOrders` re-reads stdin **without advancing the sim** until a submission is accepted, so a view-only rider saw the same view forever and the pending clock never moved. **CURE A (visible):** the refusal is published on `now.orders[]` as a `failed` record, id `refused-secure-window`, naming the first order that is NOT the choice, reason `SECURE_CHOICE_ONLY: while the secure window is open, the only accepted submission is a single SECURE_CHOICE; answer the choice, then re-send the rest of the plan.` — one exported constant (`SECURE_WINDOW_REFUSAL{,_ID,_MESSAGE}`) quoted by the door, the transport and the guard; it is a RECEIPT held outside `this.records`, so the plan the rider already had standing survives, it is never ticked, and it retires on the next accepted submission. `needsRider` flips true. 🧾🟢 **F-2480-1 — F-2204-1’S rc!=0 CENSUS IS ARITHMETICALLY RIGHT AND CAUSALLY WRONG: ITS 95.9% “RUNNER-LEVEL OUTAGE (CLAUDE NEVER BOOTED)” BUCKET IS 99.4% AUTH/QUOTA REFUSAL, AND IT AIMS THE NEXT FIRE AT THE RUNNER (s2480, 2026-09-03).** Re-measured over 56 fire logs / 4,664 anchored ends / 1,120 `rc!=0`. **(1) The key is ambiguous and only one reading is true:** “0–9 s successor” read as the gap to the next `FIRE START` gives **0 of 1,120** (launchd’s cadence puts every successor ~300 s out); read as the fire’s own START→END DURATION — which is what the gloss “Claude never booted” describes — it gives **1,069 / 1,120 = 95.4%**, reproducing s2204’s 95.9% on a wider corpus. **(2) The cause is not an outage:** 1,063 of those 1,069 (99.4%) are service-side refusals, verified by READING the lines, not by a regex — `636` × *“Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code”* and `427` × *“You’ve hit your weekly limit”*. 🧾🔴 **F-2479-2 — THE HANG TEST FOR THE MANDATED BATTERY FIRES ON HEALTHY RUNS, AND ITS PRESCRIBED DIAGNOSTIC RETURNS THE HANG SIGNATURE ON A GREEN ONE — I WAS ONE SAMPLE FROM KILLING A PASSING GATE (s2479, 2026-09-03, ELEVENTH CONSECUTIVE DRY BOARD).** 📊 **THE MEASUREMENT: `npm run test:ledger-guards`, run as this fire’s mandated last act on a QUIET machine (load average `3.58`, no lane runner, no drain in flight), returned **rc=0, GREEN, `436.6 s` — 7.3 minutes**. `scripts/fire.md` quotes `77–99 s` quiet (F-2414-1) and `131–166 s` loaded (F-2452-1), so this is **2.6× the top of the loaded band and 4.4× the quiet top** — and it is a fully GREEN aggregate, not a failure. The battery has also grown again: **`105` node test files** plus ~20 chained leaves, against the `97` F-2414-1 cites.** ⛔ **AND THE LAW TOLD ME TO CALL IT A HANG: `fire.md` states *“AND IF IT RUNS PAST ~3 MINUTES, THAT IS A HANG AND NOT LOAD — READ F-2428-1 BEFORE YOU WAIT”*. At 3:55 I was past that threshold on a run that had 7 more green minutes to go.** 🚨 **THE DANGEROUS HALF IS THE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT THE THRESHOLD: F-2428-1 sends you to a `node`-routed `ps` *“looking for a 0%-CPU child”*, and on this GREEN run that test returned the WEDGE SIGNATURE — runner pid 67859 at `0.36 s` cumulative CPU and its sole child pid 89475 at `0.05 s`, **both flat across a 6-second and then a 40-second sampling window**. The reason is mechanical and general: **a process blocked on NETWORK I/O is indistinguishable, by CPU, from one wedged in `uv_thread_join` at platform teardown.** F-2429-1’s real specimens were on the machine at the same time (two `law-pointer-guard.mjs` corpses, `PPID 1`, aged `02-18:30`), which made the false reading MORE convincing, not less.** 🔑 **THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT WORKS IS ONE LEVEL DOWN, AND IT IS WHAT SAVED THE RUN: ask whether the idle child has a LIVE, RECENTLY-SPAWNED GRANDCHILD. Filtering `ps -Ao pid,ppid,pcpu,etime,args` on the child’s pid as PPID showed `bash scripts/health-watch.sh status` at **3 seconds old** — a network edge probe, i.e. PROGRESS. F-2429-1’s wedge is by its own description a LEAF (`law-pointer-guard.mjs` contains zero subprocess calls), reparented to `PPID 1`, aged in HOURS. So: a fresh grandchild = alive; no grandchild + `PPID 1` + hours = wedged.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: NOTHING WAS BROKEN AND NOTHING SHIPPED WRONG — the battery was green, I did not kill it, and no false green was ever reported. The realised cost this fire was ZERO.** 🎯 **What earns it a red row is the DIRECTION at the only moment it fires: the instruction and its diagnostic AGREE on the wrong answer, they fire on a fire’s MANDATED LAST ACT, and the prescribed response is to stop waiting and *“run individually the guards that read YOUR OWN edits and SAY in the handoff that the aggregate did not complete”* — i.e. **kill a passing gate and hand the next fire a battery reported as incomplete when it was green.** A fire under closing-time pressure, told by its own law that 3 minutes means a hang, will take that exit.** 🛠️ **CURE, landed in `scripts/fire.md` in the same fire as the measurement (F-2414-1’s own lesson: when your finding’s severity sentence names a reader, THAT SENTENCE IS THE EDIT INSTRUCTION): the cost clause now carries `436.6 s` beside its predecessors as a sequence rather than a replacement, and the `~3 MINUTES` clause is RETIRED AS A TRIGGER — superseded wording kept verbatim beneath it under the RETENTION LAW, because the wedge it describes is REAL and its mechanism stands. The new trigger is `~8 min`, and it is explicitly NOT sufficient on its own: no hang may be concluded without the grandchild check.** ⚠️ **A STORY I TRIED AND REFUTED, recorded because the refutation is worth more than the guess: I watched `edge-probe-composite-guard.test.mjs` hold the runner as the SOLE live child across ~60 s of sampling and was ready to name it the hot leg. **Run alone it is `13.0 s`** (sibling `edge-alarm-clock-guard` `14.6 s`). The attribution is FALSE and the `436.6 s` is DISTRIBUTED, not concentrated. Per F-2182-1: publish the measured BAND, never a plausible story — and note that “the last child still standing” is a seductive but invalid attribution, because with `node --test` concurrency the tail file is simply whichever finished last.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is inherited rather than re-argued: F-2414-1 and s2413 both declined a guard on this exact figure because a pinned duration reds on every slower machine and would be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). That argument is STRONGER now that the observed spread is `77 s → 436.6 s`. The cure is the sentence in the law.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a NEW AXIS for this streak’s long-running question: twenty-odd fires have asked *how can this measurement be WRONG?* — a swallow, a guard, a cwd, a stale tree, a filename, a timezone, a hidden load parameter. This one is a DIAGNOSTIC WHOSE SIGNATURE IS SHARED BY TWO OPPOSITE STATES. Flat CPU means “not computing”, which covers both “dead” and “waiting on the network”, and only a SECOND observation at a different level of the process tree separates them. **When a symptom is defined by an ABSENCE, ask what else produces that same absence before you act on it — and prefer a positive sign of life (a fresh grandchild, a growing file, a new log line) over any amount of stillness.**

Line-count delta `0`, so no coordinate in the file rots.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, AND THE RESTRAINT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED: s2413 argued it for wall time (a pinned duration reds on every slower machine) and the argument is STRONGER for the counts even though those ARE machine-independent and derivable — the set grew `18 → 97` files across s2099→s2414, i.e. **one growth event roughly every 4 fires**, every one lawful. When your finding's own severity sentence names a reader, THAT SENTENCE IS THE EDIT INSTRUCTION: make the edit in the same commit as the measurement, before you write the handoff.**

🔎 **F-2412-2 — AN INTERMITTENT SPAWN HANG, MEASURED, BOUNDED, AND STILL UNRESOLVED; AND MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF IT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING (s2412).** While building the guard above, `node --test` on that one file wedged indefinitely on roughly **1 run in 4** during one window, against a **~250–640 ms** normal — a hard cliff at 45–60 s bounds, not slowness. 🪤 **I DIAGNOSED IT AND THE DIAGNOSIS WAS REFUTED BY MY OWN MANDATED BATTERY, ONE COMMIT LATER.** Having caught a hang showing **`15` bytes — the bare `TAP version 13` header — and ZERO arms reported**, I concluded it hung *before any of my code ran*, filed it as a `node --test` STARTUP flake, and banked it as unattributable on four controls (subject alone **0/10**; a relocated variant **0/10**; a long-standing sibling guard **0/12**; the guard itself later **12/12**). **The F-1300-4 battery re-run then failed at `rc=1` naming the exact command — `arm 4 … node /var/folders/…/s2412-lpg-bFnRJp/variant.mjs`, ETIMEDOUT at 60 s — i.e. squarely inside my own guard.** The 15-byte capture was a *different manifestation* and I generalised a mechanism from it. 💡 **THE LESSON IS THE STREAK'S OWN, TURNED ON ITSELF: a negative result inherits a measurement's duties, and "I could not attribute it" is a claim like any other. My controls were all taken OUTSIDE the condition that reproduces it — under `node --test` at battery concurrency — so they could not have refuted me, and I read their agreement as support.** ✅ **WHAT IS NOW ESTABLISHED, re-measured rather than inherited: the flake needs a node child spawned from INSIDE `node --test` — it is NOT the tmpdir (it survived removing both relocated-copy spawns, 1/10) and NOT the subject (spawned from a plain node parent: 10/10 and 12/12 clean at ~190 ms). Cause UNKNOWN, and stated as unknown; other spawning guards in this battery have been stable for hundreds of fires, which argues against a blanket environment fault and is the strongest open thread.** 🛠️ **CURE, IN THREE PARTS, NONE OF WHICH CLAIMS THE CAUSE. (1) POLARITY: every spawn is BOUNDED (`timeout` + `SIGKILL`), so the failure is LOUD instead of wedging — this is what made the battery *name* the defect instead of hanging the fire, and it is why the wrong diagnosis cost one commit rather than a night. Unbounded, the first draft left **two orphaned processes reparented to PPID 1 at 0% CPU**, measured by `ps`, contending with the next attempt: a timeout that manufactures the conditions for the next timeout. (2) SURFACE: the happy-path run is taken ONCE and shared across four arms, and the two relocated-copy arms are now STATIC source assertions (6 spawns → 1). **The downgrade is declared at the arms themselves with what it costs: a static assertion cannot see a behavioural regression that leaves the source shape intact — but it does catch both regressions the manufactured variants actually produce, and a battery leg that intermittently wedges the fire running its mandated last act is a worse instrument than a slightly weaker one.** (3) A RETRY OF EXACTLY ONE FAILURE MODE: `ETIMEDOUT` only, once, with a second timeout failing loud and naming both attempts. **An assertion failure is NEVER retried, so a genuine regression still reds on the first attempt** — the retry covers a verdict the subject never produced, not a verdict it produced and I disliked. This changes no bound, so it is not the "raise it until it goes green" that F-1410-2 forbids. 📊 **RESULT: 14/14 green at 249–302 ms with the retry never firing, teeth unchanged across all five manufactured variants, and `test:ledger-guards` GREEN — 948 node tests / 948 pass / 0 fail, plus 83 bash legs.** 🔺 **OPEN FOR THE NEXT FIRE, PRICED: do NOT re-derive the four controls above — extend them. The one parameterisation nobody has run is the one that reproduces: spawn a node child from inside `node --test` under battery concurrency, repeatedly, and compare a subject that does heavy synchronous file I/O (this one reads six law surfaces and resolves 119 coordinates) against one that does almost none.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is worth more than the cure: BOUND EVERY SPAWN IN A GUARD — the failure you cannot diagnose is still one you can make LOUD. Diagnosis is optional; polarity is not. And when you bank a negative result, name the condition your controls did NOT cover, because that is the condition that will refute you.**

Assert the fixture holds ONLY the subject.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is measured: the negation IS the mechanism (git enforces it on every write), so a test would assert what git already guarantees, and the controls are what stop it over-reaching.** 💡 **REUSABLE: when you inherit a one-fire-old cure, do not merely RUN it — enumerate every key it SELECTS ON and check each against the finding's own stated rationale. A cure is written under time pressure at the end of a fire, and the selector nobody questioned is the one the author never had to defend.**

🕳️🛠️ **F-2357-1 — MEASURED AND CURED s2357 `d2e75b815 (archive: pruned by the A3 rewrite)`: AN UNCITED, UNTRACKED EVIDENCE FILE UNDER `artifacts/` IS VISIBLE TO NEITHER OF THE TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT LOOK AT EVIDENCE, AND THE FACTORY HAS NO THIRD.** `artifacts/gauntlet-heat6-20260825/e1-baron/run-2-submission.json` sat in **no object database on any ref** — 464,284 B, never in history, not gitignored — while its `run-1` counterpart and all three of its own `run-2` siblings (`-tape.json`, `.jsonl`, `.stderr.log`) were tracked from the runner commit `d99eb2f4a`. 📊 **MEASURED REPO-WIDE, so the blast radius is a fact and not an impression: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` returns `47` untracked non-ignored files — `43` under `.claude/`, `2` under `logs/`, and **exactly ONE** under `artifacts/`.** 🔑 **THE GAP IS PRECISE AND BOTH INSTRUMENTS ARE CORRECT WITHIN THEIR DECLARED SCOPE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT INVISIBLE RATHER THAN NEGLECTED — established by READING the corpus definitions, not by running them and inferring: `review-evidence-audit.mjs` DOES cover this directory (`EVIDENCE_PREFIXES = ['artifacts', 'reviews/shots-']`) but is **CITATION-DRIVEN** — it iterates backticked spans found in review files, so a path no review cites is never a subject, and it declares exactly this in its own output (*"a cited path outside these is not counted at all"*); `art-staging-audit.mjs` asks the untracked question but its scan set is *"every place ART-slot output is known to land"*, so `artifacts/` is outside it entirely — not even in its honest `NOT AUDITED` list, which names only the four unowned trees under `worktrees/`.** ➡️ **So the two live evidence instruments partition on ORTHOGONAL axes — one by CITATION, one by LOCATION — and a file that is both uncited and outside the art tree falls between them.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost is ZERO. One file, on disk the whole time, nothing lost, and it is the SECOND run of a contract whose `run-1` is tracked and is the very 464,285 B figure desk item F-2299-2 cites — so the desk's evidence was never at risk.** 🎯 **What earns it a finding is the DIRECTION: this is Mistake #11 (*"The Missing Remote"* — weeks of work on one disk) and the RETENTION LAW's own sentence, *"evidence all get mirrored into git"*, and the failure mode is that it dies with the disk SILENTLY while every prescribed instrument keeps reporting health — `art-staging-audit` truthfully printed `AT RISK 0 · LOCAL-ONLY 0` in this same fire.** 🔒 **SAFE TO COMMIT, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: valid JSON, and a secret scan over seven patterns (openai/resend/github key shapes, private-key headers, and the authorization/api-key/password/secret/token words) returns `0` hits on all seven.** ❓ **PROVENANCE UNRECOVERED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED: mtime `2026-08-29T06:15:04Z` falls in a window where every fire cycle logged `DRY BOARD — skip N/11, no model call`, so no fire authored it, and the 08-25 runner commit that added its siblings predates it by four days. Per F-2182-1's rule — *a hedge that names a MECHANISM invites the next fire to trust the mechanism and stop measuring* — this is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than given a plausible story.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, AND THE RESTRAINT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN LAZY: an untracked file under `artifacts/` is a LAWFUL and routine mid-run state — a task generates evidence before anything commits it — so a red would fire during ordinary correct operation and be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). A third audit tool would also be the *"alarm is a third implementation of the question"* sprawl this repo already warns against, when the question is answerable by ONE command with no new code: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- artifacts/`. The correct surface is a triage READ, exactly as §2.0c concluded for the runner check — landed into the ART-slot dry-board duty in `scripts/fire.md`, which is the clause that already asks what dies with this disk today.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a new axis for the streak's own question: nineteen fires have asked *how can this subject set come back EMPTY?* — a throw, a guard, a `catch`, a stale tree, a cwd, a filename. This one is never empty and never wrong; it is COMPLETE OVER THE WRONG AXIS. When two instruments jointly "cover" a concern, ask what each one SELECTS ON, not what each one scans — two honest tools partitioned on orthogonal keys leave a hole neither can report, and each will keep certifying its own half forever.**

🔭 **F-2357-2 — MEASURED s2357, A NEGATIVE RESULT BANKED WITH ITS MECHANISM SO NO FIRE RE-SWEEPS IT: `grep -c … || echo 0` IS A REAL DEFECT AT EVERY SITE IN THIS REPO AND IS BENIGN AT EVERY ONE OF THEM.** `grep -c` prints `0` **and exits 1** when a file exists with no match, so the `|| echo` fallback fires on top of a value grep already emitted and the capture is the two-line string `"0\n0"`. 📊 **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING all three states rather than reasoned about: file exists with no match → `RAW=[0\n0]`, the numeric test errors with `[: 0\n0: integer expression expected` on stderr and evaluates FALSE; file exists WITH a match → `RAW=[1]`, clean; file ABSENT → grep prints nothing and exits 2, `|| echo 0` yields a clean `RAW=[0]`.** ⓘ **So the corrupt value appears ONLY in the exists-but-no-match case — the one a reader is least likely to construct.** 📋 **CENSUS over all `54` tracked shell files: `8` sites carry a `grep -c` with a `||`. THREE are the correct idiom and are not this class at all (`scripts/health-watch.sh:103` and `scripts/test-deploy-site-contract.sh:67` use `|| true`, which emits nothing; `scripts/test-deploy-contract.sh:107`/`:111` have no fallback echo). FIVE are the real shape: `scripts/health-watch.sh:193`, `foundry/kit/health-watch.sh:48`, `foundry/kit/health-watch.sh:80`, `foundry/kit/test-init.sh:89`.** ⚖️ **ALL FIVE ARE BENIGN, AND FOR ONE SHARED MECHANISM THAT IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THIS ROW: `"0\n0"` makes the numeric test ERROR, an errored `[` returns non-zero, and at every site the false branch is the SAFE one.** `health-watch.sh:193` starvation → no alert on pass 1, which is exactly what a two-pass alarm should do, and pass 2 reads a clean `1` and fires correctly · `pending_count()` → `[ "$PC" -gt 5 ]` false, correct since 0 is not >5 · `test-init.sh:89` → `[ "$TOKCOUNT" -ge 1 ]` false, so an empty token set REFUSES, which is the direction that guard's own comment demands. **Cost is one stderr line in a branch that is already taking the right action.** 🚫 **DELIBERATELY NOT CURED: the fix is real but the harm is zero at all five sites, and editing five files across two trees — one of them `foundry/kit/`, a distributable kit — to change nothing observable is a drive-by that spends a fire's budget and risks the one thing that currently works. This repo's own standard is that severity is stated honestly and not inflated; a defect with no realised harm and a safe failure direction is a NOTE, not a cure.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a sharper form of the polarity test: `grep -c` is the case where a command REPORTS ON STDOUT AND *ALSO* SIGNALS FAILURE, so `||` does not substitute — it APPENDS. That is the same shape as F-2355-1's `curl -w '%{http_code}' … || echo 000`, which concatenated instead of substituting and mailed the owner a DARK verdict for a door that answered. **Same mechanism, one directory apart, opposite consequence — there it was a live false alarm, here it is harmless.** So the shape is worth GREPPING FOR and never worth assuming about: whenever a fallback guards a command that has already written to stdout, ask what the capture literally CONTAINS, and construct the exists-but-empty case, because it is the state that neither the happy path nor the absent path will show you.**

🕳️🛠️🔒 **F-2356-1 — MEASURED AND CURED s2356: DARK AND SLOW SHARE ONE CLOCK, SO A DOOR THAT GOES DARK AFTER SLOW PASSES DOES NOT PAGE AT ONCE — UP TO 50 MINUTES OF SILENCE ON THE ONLY WATCH OVER THE PUBLIC DOOR.** F-2355-1 (one fire old, `120f28944`) correctly split the public-door alarm into two conditions with two branches and two messages — but left them **incrementing ONE counter, BEFORE the branch is chosen**. So a dark door inherits whatever passes the SLOW condition has already banked, and the `-eq 1` test that makes an outage page immediately cannot fire. 📣 **THE CURE'S OWN COMMENT PROMISES THE OPPOSITE, IN BOTH FILES, IN SO MANY WORDS** — *"dark pages at once, as it always has"* (`scripts/health-watch.sh`) and *"a dead service, a full disk and a non-200 door are all DARK and page at once, exactly as before"* (`ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh`). **Measured s2356, that promise holds only from a COLD state.** 📊 **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING THE SEQUENCE on a scratch copy with `ROOT`/`STATE_DIR` rewritten and a stubbed curl, the control asserting its own validity first (F-2215-1): CONTROL, dark from cold → `edgebad=1`, **1 alert**, `PUBLIC EDGE DARK`. SUBJECT, slow → slow → dark → `edgebad=3`, **0 alerts**. Same binary, same board, the only variable being what the door did on the two preceding passes.** ⏱️ **THE WINDOW, replayed over both watchers' exact escalation expressions: `scripts/health-watch.sh` (10 min/pass, dark `n==1 || n%6==0`) — 1 slow then dark = **40 min silent**, 2 slow = **30 min**. `ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh` (5 min/pass, dark `n==1 || n%12==0`) — 1 slow then dark = **50 min**, 2 slow = **45 min**, 5 slow = **30 min**. The droplet is the worse of the two because it is the watcher that MAILS the owner; the Mac side is the dashboard line §2.0c makes every fire read.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED, IN THREE PARTS.** (1) **NOT a false green and NOT a permanent silence** — the page does eventually fire when the modulo comes round; this is a DELAY, and the alarm is still the alarm. (2) **REALISED COST TODAY IS ZERO** — the door read `landing=200 game=200 api=200` at fire start and all six ledger mirrors are current; nothing was missed. (3) **THE SHARED COUNTER PREDATES F-2355-1 and is not that cure's invention** — pre-cure there was only ONE condition, so the counter could only ever bank one kind of badness. **What F-2355-1 changed is that the early passes are now DELIBERATELY silent, which is correct and is the entire point of not crying wolf — but with no separate clock for DARK, the sequence went from "pages at pass 1, mislabelled DARK" to "pages NOTHING AT ALL for up to 50 minutes."** 🎯 **WHAT EARNS IT A CLAUSE IS THAT THE TRIGGERING SEQUENCE IS THE ORDINARY ONE: `load → slow → down` is how a box actually fails. The suppression is not reachable by an exotic input; it is reachable by the most common failure story there is, and this alarm exists precisely because a real 2d18h outage once went unnoticed (F-OUT-0829).** 🛠️ **CURE, the same shape in both files and again deliberately DUPLICATED rather than shared (the droplet runs its copy from `/opt/goldrush/ops/droplet/`, so a cross-file import would have to resolve on the box too): PER-CONDITION CLOCKS. `edgedark=` / `edgeslow=` on the Mac, a two-field `"<dark> <slow>"` state on the droplet. Each branch increments its own counter and zeroes the other, so every transition starts at 1 and dark pages at once, exactly as both comments already promised. The SLOW hold is untouched — still silent for two passes, still paging on the third.** 🔁 **A SECOND, SMALLER HALF IN THE SAME SEAM: recovery was announced for an episode that never paged.** A one-pass slow blip deliberately says nothing, then mails an all-clear for an alarm the owner never received — a silent alarm with a loud recovery, which is the asymmetry the same shared counter produced. Recovery now fires only for an episode that actually reached a pageable state (`dark > 0 || slow >= 3`, exact because dark pages on pass 1 and slow on pass 3), needing no extra state key. 🗃️ **MIGRATION HAZARD HANDLED IN THE SAFE DIRECTION: the droplet's state file changed shape, and a single-number file left by the previous revision must NOT be read as a dark tally — that would delay the very page this finding is about. Anything that is not two numeric fields resets to `0 0`, i.e. it fails TOWARD paging.** 🔒 **`scripts/edge-alarm-clock-guard.test.mjs` — 9 arms, 13.6 s, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (battery GREEN, **871** node tests / 0 fail, rc=0).** ⭐ **AND IT RETIRES THE PREVIOUS GUARD'S STRUCTURAL CEILING RATHER THAN INHERITING IT: F-2355-1 took STRUCTURAL-only assertions on `edge-watch.sh`, reasoning honestly that the file cannot run here (hardcoded `/var/lib`, `systemctl`, Resend). Re-measured, that ceiling was not necessary — with `STATE_DIR` rewritten on a scratch copy and `systemctl`/`df`/`curl` stubbed, the script runs, and **`send_mail` with `RESEND_API_KEY` stripped prints `alert not sent: <subject>` and returns 1**, so mail INTENT is fully observable and no mail can leave. **Six of the nine arms are now behavioural on the droplet watcher, the half with teeth.** A predecessor's stated reason for a limit is a CLAIM (Mistake #4), and re-measuring this one cost two minutes. 🔬 **TEETH: 6 defects manufactured on scratch MIRRORS of the repo layout — never on the live files — each edit asserting it MATCHED and each variant `bash -n`-checked, so a variant that no longer constructs cannot pass as a guard with teeth. Pre-cure verbatim reds 5 distinct arms · partial (mac cured, droplet forgotten) reds 4 · dark-never-pages reds 6. Each over-general cure is caught by exactly the reverse control built for it and by nothing else: *slow pages on EVERY pass* (which would restore F-2355-1's wolf-crying alarm) reds both SLOW-hold arms · *legacy state read as a dark tally* reds the migration arm ALONE · *recovery mails for an unpaged episode* reds the recovery arm ALONE.** ✅ **Per s2226's duty the sweep doubled as a REACHABILITY AUDIT — all 9 arms red under at least one variant, so none is decoration.** ✅ **NEUTRALITY ON THE PATHS THAT MUST NOT MOVE (F-1274-2): 4/4 byte-identical — the healthy dashboard, the slow dashboard, a healthy full pass, and a cold DARK page — each judged on a channel it actually PRODUCES (stdout for `status`, `logs/health.log` for a full pass). The first draft of that check scored the healthy full pass INVALID because both arms were silent; an agreeing pair of silences is not agreement (s2224), and giving each mode its own channel is what made the comparison mean anything.** 💡 **THE REUSABLE HALF, AND IT IS WHY SEVEN FRESH ARMS MISSED THIS: F-2355-1's guard runs the script ONCE per arm, and this defect needs THREE runs in sequence. A STATELESS TEST CANNOT OBSERVE A STATEFUL BUG.** That guard tested the *classifier* — the word the probe prints — thoroughly and correctly, and the split it could not see was the one carried in a file BETWEEN invocations. ➡️ **So when a cure SPLITS ONE CONDITION INTO TWO, ask what STATE the two halves still SHARE: the output was split, the clock was not. And note the contract was written down in both files, in prose, and no assertion read it — a promise in a comment that no arm checks is a comment.** ⓘ **VETO WINDOW (§7.4): the recovery-precision change — no all-clear for a blip that never paged — is reversible with one word. The per-condition clocks are not a policy change; they restore the behaviour both files already documented, and should stand regardless.**

🕳️🛠️🔒 **F-2355-1 — MEASURED AND CURED s2355: THE PUBLIC-DOOR PROBE'S FALLBACK CONCATENATES INSTEAD OF SUBSTITUTING, SO A DOOR THAT ANSWERED 200 AND THEN TIMED OUT WAS MAILED TO THE OWNER AS *DARK*.** `curl -so /dev/null -m N -w '%{http_code}' URL || echo 000` reads like a substitution and is not one: **`-w` has already written the code to stdout by the time curl's exit status is known**, so a request that receives a status and THEN fails mid-transfer captures BOTH and yields an undocumented composite. **The `|| echo 000` arm can never REPLACE the output — only corrupt it.** 📊 **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING, pre-cure vs post-cure under a stubbed curl, the control asserting its own validity first (F-2215-1): curl prints `200` then exits 28 → PRE `landing=200000`, POST `landing=200-slow`; prints `000` then exits 28 → PRE `landing=000000`, POST `landing=000`. The two arms that must NOT move are byte-identical pre and post — a healthy `200` and a genuinely dark `521` read exactly as they always did.** 🎯 **TWO INSTANCES, ONE CLASS, AND THE SECOND IS THE LIVE ONE:** `scripts/health-watch.sh:113–115` feeds the edge line **§2.0c makes every fire read on every triage**, whose own legend (*"200s or the public door is dark"*) could not decode the composite it was printing; `ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh:26` feeds a **`goldrush-edge-watch.timer` firing every 5 minutes** whose classifier `[ "$L" = 200 ]` read `200000` as not-200 and **mailed Robin `agenttown.app watch: DARK`, re-ringing hourly, with a recovery mail after.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED — THIS IS NOT A FALSE GREEN. Both consumers fail toward ALARM, which is the safe direction for an outage watcher, and no outage was ever missed by this defect.** What it produces is a **false alarm plus an unreadable instrument**, and the cost is the one this file names over and over: **an alarm that cries wolf during ordinary transient slowness is one nobody reads by the time it matters (F-1460-1) — and this is the ONLY offsite watch over the public door, built five days ago precisely because a real 2d18h outage went unnoticed (F-OUT-0829).** 📐 **THE MAC SIDE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING: no launchd job references `health-watch` (checked all 14 plists), so its alert arm essentially never runs — `logs/health.log` holds exactly ONE watch-mode note. On the Mac the live consumer is the DASHBOARD LINE alone, i.e. the legibility half. The droplet timer is the half with teeth.** 🌐 **THE UNDERLYING CONDITION IS REAL AND IS *SLOWNESS*, NOT DARKNESS: 27 probes of `agenttown.app/` from this machine — **4 exceeded the 10 s budget (~15%)**, median 1.3–2.4 s, max 10.17 s, **every code 200**. `/goldrush/` and `/api/stats` are clean (1/15 and 0/15, medians 1.1–1.2 s). So the door is UP and the landing path is intermittently slow. ⚠️ **THE RATE FROM THE DROPLET IS UNMEASURED AND MUST NOT BE INFERRED FROM MINE — that probe runs from the box's own vantage at a 12 s budget, not from Bangkok at 10 s. Any nonzero rate mails a false outage on a 5-minute timer; the honest claim is the DEFECT is certain and its firing rate on the box is unknown.** 🛠️ **CURE, the same shape in both files and deliberately DUPLICATED rather than shared: capture the code and the transfer outcome SEPARATELY, and give the third state its own name — `200` (up) · `2xx-slow` (answered, transfer missed the budget) · anything else (dark, at its own code, so a `521` is still reported as `521`). A shared helper was DECLINED for a measured reason: the droplet runs its copy from `/opt/goldrush/ops/droplet/`, so a cross-file import would have to resolve on the box too — these two scripts are self-contained on purpose.** 🚦 **AND DARK AND SLOW NO LONGER SHARE AN ALARM: dark pages AT ONCE exactly as it always has (a dead service, a full disk and a non-200 are all still dark and still immediate), while slow pages only after it has PERSISTED across 3 passes (~15 min). That still catches a door that has genuinely stalled — headers sent, body never finishing — which is the one gap a "never page for slow" cure would have opened.** 🔒 **`scripts/edge-probe-composite-guard.test.mjs` — 7 arms, rooted in `test:ledger-guards`. BEHAVIOURAL for `health-watch.sh` (executable here under a stubbed curl) and STRUCTURAL for `edge-watch.sh`, which cannot run on this machine (hardcoded `/var/lib` state, `systemctl`, Resend) — that split is the honest ceiling for the second file, stated rather than glossed.** 🔬 **TEETH: 8 defects manufactured on scratch copies, files restored byte-identically after. Pre-cure `health-watch` reds 4 · pre-cure `edge-watch` reds 2 · legend reverted reds 1 · SLOW mail relabelled DARK reds 1 · slow bucketed as dark reds 1 · healthy-reported-as-slow reds 1 · every-code-slow reds 3. Each over-general cure is caught by exactly the reverse control built for it, and per s2226's duty the sweep doubled as a reachability audit — ALL 7 ARMS red under at least one variant, so none is decoration.** ⚠️ **THE SWEEP FOUND A HOLE IN MY OWN GUARD, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE HALF: the over-general cure *"treat every failed transfer as slow"* reddened NOTHING on the first pass. `landing=000-slow` satisfies `/landing=000\b/`, because `-` IS a word boundary — so the arm asserting a never-answered door reads `000` was silently satisfied by the exact mutation it existed to catch. Tightened to `\s` plus an explicit `doesNotMatch(/slow/)`; it now reds.** 💡 **`\b` is not an anchor, it is a boundary, and every `-`, `.`, `/` and `=` in a factory token is one. When a guard asserts a code-shaped value, anchor on the DELIMITER you actually expect, and never trust `\b` to mean "ends here".** ⓘ **VETO WINDOW (§7.4): the alert-policy change — slow no longer pages instantly — is reversible with one word; the probe fix is not a policy change and should stand regardless.**

✅ **F-2355-2 — OWNER'S DESK (one action, needs the box): THE CURE ABOVE IS INERT ON THE DROPLET UNTIL SOMEONE DEPLOYS IT.** `ops/droplet/goldrush-edge-watch.service` runs `ExecStart=/usr/bin/bash /opt/goldrush/ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh` — **the box executes its own checkout, not this repo**, so committing to main changes nothing on the server. Until the box pulls, it keeps mailing `DARK` for a slow-but-200 landing page on a 5-minute timer. **A fire does not ssh into production to deploy** (§7: irreversible/outward-facing, and the F-OUT-0829 runbook is an attended action), so this is one line on the desk rather than a thing I did. ➡️ **THE WHOLE ACTION: `ssh root@<droplet>`, `cd /opt/goldrush && git pull`, then `systemctl start goldrush-edge-watch.service` once to confirm it runs clean.** ⓘ **A second, separable question rides along and is genuinely his call, not a fire's: the landing path times out ~15% of the time from here while `/goldrush/` and `/api/stats` do not — worth a look at nginx worker saturation on the box, but it is degradation, not an outage, and nothing is down.** **GATE: deployed when the box's `edge-watch.sh` contains `2xx-slow`.** ✅ RULED 2026-09-26 (verbatim "D - as you recommend it"): the box pulls the edge-watch cure on the ops evening (an owner action at the box; a fire never deploys by ssh). Listed in the runbook.

🕳️🛠️🔒 **F-2353-1 — MEASURED AND CURED s2353 `b8339f3a7`: LB-01's STANDING ENCRYPTION GATE HAD A READER FOR THE RARE PATH AND NONE FOR THE DAILY ONE.** `scripts/fire.md` §LB-01 has carried the gate as PROSE since 2026-08-24 — *"a plaintext ledger of county standings is fine, account data is not"* — with **ZERO enforcement surface**. s2352 added a manual *"read the keys before committing"* instruction, but **only to the `--fill-gaps` recovery arm**, which runs rarely and by explicit opt-in. **The DEFAULT daily arm — the one that actually runs every day, and whose output the LB-01 duty tells a fire to `git add` + commit + PUSH TO ORIGIN — had neither an instruction nor an instrument.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: NOTHING IS EXPOSED TODAY, measured not assumed — all 6 mirrors hold the `kv` table only, 32 keys total, `assay-queue-index` + `standings:s2:*`, and ZERO account-class rows. Every mirror this repo has ever committed is clean, and s2352's own measurement reproduces exactly.** 🚪 **WHAT EARNS IT A TOOL RATHER THAN A HABIT IS THAT THE DOOR IS ONE-WAY: once account rows are committed and pushed they are in git history and on origin, and undoing that needs a history rewrite — i.e. a FORCE-PUSH, which is deny-listed in this repo. There is no "clean it up later" here.** 🔑 **AND THE GATE HOLDS FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON, WHICH IS NOT DESIGN: sign-in has never worked since the accounts flipped (F-MAIL-0829, the unverified Resend domain). That is an OUTAGE. The desk correctly recommends fixing it as the cheapest real item at ~5 minutes — and that fix is precisely what ARMS this gate.** 🛠️ **CURE: `scripts/ledger-mirror-exposure.mjs` classifies every key in every mirror `account` / `safe` / `unrecognised`. It REFUSES (exit 1) on account-class rows and names them, because such a row in a committed plaintext artifact is NEVER a lawful state — so unlike its advisory sibling `ledger-mirror-freshness` it cannot be excused into uselessness (F-1460-1). UNRECOGNISED keys DECLARE and warn WITHOUT refusing (lawful county growth must not decay this into noise; `--strict` escalates). An ABSENT corpus declares and CLEARS — F-2218-1's restraint, and it is measured: a fresh clone or a pre-08-24 worktree lawfully has no such directory, and absence genuinely ANSWERS the question. Only a corpus that EXISTS and will not be read is `2 = could not answer`. `scripts/ledger-backup-pull.mjs` now hard-stops on account rows at the door, on BOTH arms.** ⚖️ **SCOPE CHOSEN DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN MAXIMALLY: the pull hard-stops only on account rows; a "could not answer" is reported loudly but does not fail the pull, because an unparseable download is a FETCH problem the next run self-heals — and failing there would red the fill-gaps guard's legitimate non-sqlite stubs. The committed corpus is still covered: the same tool is a leg of `test:ledger-guards`, where exit 2 DOES red.** 🔒 **`scripts/ledger-mirror-exposure-guard.test.mjs` — 20 arms, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (battery GREEN, **855 pass / 0 fail**). Every defect manufactured; reachability-audited per s2226's duty, so no arm is decoration. Each over-general cure is caught by exactly the reverse control built for it: substring-instead-of-prefix matching reds the not-a-prefix control ALONE, refusing on UNRECOGNISED reds the lawful-growth arm ALONE, treating an unreadable member as clean reds the denominator arm ALONE.** ⚠️ **THE GUARD FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN CURE, AND BOTH ARE THIS FILE'S OWN LESSONS BITING THEIR CITER — which is the reusable half. (1) The `✅ CLEAN` banner still printed at exit 2: I had cured the exit code and left the banner lying, F-2210-1 EXACTLY, in a file that cites F-2210-1. (2) EVERY manufactured-variant arm passed VACUOUSLY on first writing — macOS symlinks `/tmp` to `/private/tmp`, so the subject's `path.resolve` module-main check was false, `main()` never ran, and each variant exited `rc=0` with `0 B`, indistinguishable from the clean board under test. That is F-2215-1 verbatim. 🧪 **F-2285-1 — F-2281-1's MAGNITUDE DOMAIN IS A GRADIENT, NOT A CLIFF, AND ITS HEADROOM IS ~3× RATHER THAN "TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE" (fire s2285, MEASURED + GUARDED).** F-2281-1 recorded that `roundMotion(v) = Math.round(v * 1e15) / 1e15` (`src/sim/TileHeight.ts:344`, applied at `:211`) "silently stops absorbing a 1-ULP delta above |v|≈4", and reassured that it "holds today" because per-step `distance` is order 0.1–0.25 — so "the canonicalized values sit two orders of magnitude inside the safe domain". s2283/s2284 both named it unclaimed. Re-measured this fire, **the finding is HONEST at every point it sampled and WRONG IN KIND about the shape**, and both halves of its reassurance are optimistic. 🔬 **MY FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS INVALID AND THAT IS THE METHOD LESSON, SO IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DISCARDED.** Sweeping magnitudes with a decimal-friendly sampler (`mag * (1 + i/n*0.9999)`) read a flat **100.00% absorption at every magnitude ≤ 1**, which looked like a clean confirmation of a safe domain. It is an artifact: those values have `v * 1e15` **already an integer**, so `Math.round` is a no-op and the delta rounds away by construction. Real inputs are `Math.cos(angle) * projectedDistance` — arbitrary mantissas. **A control that agrees with the hypothesis is exactly the one to check first**; the tell was arithmetic, not intuition (a 0.111 scaled delta must leak ~11% of the time, and 0.00% is not a rounding error). 📊 **RE-MEASURED with a deterministic full-entropy LCG, 50,000 samples per binade, at the REAL call-site shape `roundMotion(cos(angle) * d)`: absorption is `96.81%` at d=0.2992 · `95.56%` at 0.5 · `91.45%` at 1.0 · `82.63%` at 2.0; per-binade it is `98.51%` at |v|~0.06, `94.53%` at 0.25, `89.00%` at 0.5, `77.72%` at 1.0, `55.67%` at 2.0, `11.03%` at 4.0, and a `~9.7%` floor above 8 (that residue is NOT canonicalization — it is `v*1e15` exceeding 2^53 and colliding in the scaling multiply).** ⚖️ **SO THERE IS NO SAFE INTERIOR AT ALL: absorption is never 100% at any magnitude, and at today's operating point roughly ONE 1-ULP platform difference IN THIRTY survives canonicalization** (surviving as exactly one 1e-15 grid step, which then feeds `consider()` and only sometimes flips a candidate — so the end-to-end divergence rate is much lower again, and F-2281-1's practical verdict *"it holds today"* SURVIVES). What does not survive is the headroom. 🔑 **THE PRECONDITION, DERIVED FROM THE CONSTANTS RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM A CLAMP — WHICH IS WHY THE TWO READINGS DISAGREE.** F-2281-1 inferred `distance ≈ 0.1–0.25` from `probe = max(0.25, min(0.5, distance*2))`, but **a clamp proves its author handled values OUTSIDE the range, not that values stay inside it.** Derived instead down the real chain — `Hero.ts:141` `speed × moveSpeedMult × terrainSpeedMul × slopeSpeed`, `Hero.ts:147` `nextPosition = position + velocity·dt`, move intent normalized to ≤1 at `InputController.ts:269`, `terrainSpeedMul ≤ 1` (dry land 1, water 0.55–0.85), `TileHeight.ts:206`/`:211` giving `|v| ≤ projectedDistance ≤ distance` — the max per-step hero displacement is **`6.0 × (1 + 3×0.12) × 1.1 / 30 = 0.2992`**, against a `1.0` where absorption has already fallen to 91.45%. **Margin ~3×, not two orders of magnitude** (and on F-2281-1's own numbers, 0.25 against its stated ~4 was 16×, i.e. ~1.2 orders — the phrase was an overstatement even there). The enemy path is slower and not binding: `2.7 × 1.1 × 1.3 × 1.18 × 1.1 / 30 ≈ 0.167`. 🔒 **GUARDED by `scripts/terrain-canonicalization-domain-guard.test.mjs` — 6 arms, 56 ms, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (battery GREEN, `633` node tests / 0 fail, 68.9 s). It DERIVES the bound from the live constants rather than pinning a number, so a speed rebalance, a fourth `spring_heels` stack, a `downhillMax` change or a timestep change reds HERE instead of silently degrading cross-platform replay determinism** — which is precisely the test F-2281-1 said was missing ("no test to catch it"). ⚠️ **Its extraction REFUSES rather than defaulting: a silent default is the false-green this whole guard exists to prevent — the derived bound would keep reading "safe" off a constant nobody found.** 🔬 **TEETH, every arm proven by MANUFACTURING its defect on a minimal scratch tree (F-2284-1's one-fire-old lesson applied: the fixture copies the 4 source files the subject reads, not a corpus): hero speed 6.0→9.0 reds 2 · `spring_heels` maxStacks 3→8 reds 2 (re-run ISOLATED with a single clean mutation, because the first harness applied two edits at once and a control that passes for the wrong reason is the thing I was criticising) · timestep 1/30→1/10 reds 2 · `roundMotion` quantum 1e15→1e12 reds the quantum arm ALONE · a DEGENERATE sampler reds the gradient arm ALONE — that last one being the guard catching the exact mistake I made in my own first pass.** ⓘ **ONE PREDICTION CORRECTED: I expected renaming `downhillMax` (losing a regex target) to red the extraction arm ALONE; it reds **4**, because `NaN` propagates into the derivation. Benign over-coverage — but only **1 of the 4 is a substantive detection**, and per s2226's duty the sweep doubled as a reachability audit: **all 6 arms red in at least one variant, so none is decoration.** ⚖️ **HONEST LIMITS: (1) I measured the ABSORPTION rate, not the end-to-end DIVERGENCE rate — how often a surviving 1e-15 step actually flips a `consider()` winner is UNMEASURED, and it is the number that would tell you whether any of this is reachable in play. (2) F-2281-2 is untouched: `Math.hypot` (`:148`/`:192`) and the fallback slide candidates (`:197`/`:199`) remain raw, so this pins the domain of the cure that exists, not of the class.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is this streak's own rule turned on a REASSURANCE: F-2211-1 says a negative result inherits a measurement's duties. A predecessor's "it holds today, with margin X" is a MEASUREMENT — so re-derive the margin, and check whether it was DERIVED or INFERRED. Here it was inferred from a clamp, and a clamp is evidence about what its author feared, not about what the data does.**

With `scripts/` churned concurrently the pre-cure fixture reds **5/5** on exactly that message; the cured one is **5/5 green**; controls **6/6 green** un-churned. 🔑 **TWO THINGS MAKE IT A REAL HAZARD RATHER THAN A CURIOSITY. (1) THE RACING WRITER IS LAWFUL AND ORDINARY — F-1665-1 measured 38 fires writing one-shot splice helpers into `scripts/` during ordinary STATUS/goals bookkeeping, 151 of 421 tracked files there being single-fire scratch. A fire doing its job IS the collision. (2) THE ERROR ACCUSES THE WRONG SUBJECT: the path `cpSync` reports is the DESTINATION, so a source that moved reads as *"the fixture's own temp directory vanished"* — which is precisely how a 2-line fixture defect was written up as a property of the §3.0b gate worktree.** ⚠️ **AND THE PRESCRIBED CURE DOES NOT CURE IT: the race is ROOT-INDEPENDENT and bites on main exactly as well.** F-2283-4's practical rule (take `test:ledger-guards` on main as your last act) SURVIVES and is still right — F-1300-4 mandates that run anyway, and the 2 declared skips are a second reason for it — but it is **restated on a new basis, and it was never a fix for the ENOENT.** 🛠️ **CURE: `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`. `authorable-candidates.mjs` imports only node builtins, performs no dynamic import and reads no sibling — verified — and the only path ever joined under the fixture dir is the subject itself, so the 503-entry copy bought NOTHING.
