Each over-general cure is caught by exactly the control built for it and reds exactly ONE arm: a blanket `cpSync` ban → the single-file control ALONE · dropping comment-stripping → the class assertion ALONE · narrowing the corpus to empty → the corpus declaration ALONE, with its `ran=false` proving the declaration line vanished, this streak's signature failure.** ⓘ **All four predictions held this fire, which has not been true recently — recorded as one data point, not as evidence the reverse-control sweep can be skipped.** 🚫 **DELIBERATELY NO BEHAVIOURAL RACE ARM: reproducing the ENOENT needs ~300 files churned in the live `scripts/` directory, which a gate battery must never do, and a timing-dependent arm greens on a loaded machine.** ⚠️ **HONEST LIMITS, BOTH OF THEM: (1) I proved the MECHANISM, not the FREQUENCY — my churn was aggressive (300 files, continuous for the subject's lifetime) where a real fire writes one helper, so this is consistent with s2283's run 1 but does not prove it is what happened. (2) THE 14-MINUTE HANG REMAINS UNDIAGNOSED — my race produced reds, never a hang; the 0.0%-CPU flat-line is still the tell, and s1536's ~19-minute hang while overlapping two batteries on shared `claimed-spec-harness-guard`/`fixture-teardown` fixtures remains the closest known relative.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is Mistake #4 pointed at an ERROR MESSAGE rather than at a claim: an exception names the operation that failed, not the thing that caused it — `cpSync` reports its DESTINATION while the SOURCE is what moved. A whole-corpus copy in a fixture is a standing invitation for this: it makes every file in a live, concurrently-written directory an input to a test that needs exactly one of them.**

Two hazards, stacked, both PERMISSIVE: **(1)** `rowId()` used the unanchored `FINDING`, so a row about `F-CLAW-2X` was keyed `F-CLAW-2` — an id that is not in the row, i.e. **F-2229-1's defect in the sibling file, on the identical question about an identical subject**; **(2)** `analyse()` then satisfied that key with `tail.includes(id)`, a RAW SUBSTRING test, so ANY desk id sharing the prefix answered for it. **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING, not by a green** (5 arms driving the exported pure core, each asserting it reached `kind:'window'` with its row recognised as owner-gated): desk carrying only the PARENT `F-CLAW-2` + new owner-gated row keyed `F-CLAW-2X` → **NOT FLAGGED**; desk carrying only the longer `F-2131-1b` + row keyed `F-2131-1` → **NOT FLAGGED**. On the REAL qualifying set — the 68 owner-gated rows of 1988 in `BACKLOG.md` — substring and whole-token containment disagree on ZERO of 1402 desk tails, so every verdict this guard has ever printed was TRUE, verified not assumed. Over ALL rows the disagreement is 351 pairs, but that is an upper bound on a set this guard never asks about, and reporting it as the severity would be inflation** (my own first pass nearly did: the loudest names in it — `blocked`, `building`, `scripts` — are slug keys from NON-owner-gated rows, and the three bare-word slugs that DO qualify turned out to be commit hashes, not English words). Both ingredients have occurred separately — five sub-ids have sat on desks, two desks carried an id shadowed by a longer one — but never yet together with a row birth. 🛠️ **CURE: import the row-key grammar F-2229-1 already ruled on rather than write a fifth copy (F-2227-1: four independent copies is HOW this predicate drifted), exported from `desk-declaration-guard.mjs` as a non-global twin DERIVED from `FINDING_ROW.source`, so it cannot drift from its original by construction.** The desk side becomes `carriesId()`, and **the distinction that makes it safe is the one s2229's refutation turns on: `carriesId` never ENUMERATES desk ids, so unlike widening the desk-TAIL scan — measured by s2229 to invent three items with no row across 1457 desks — it CANNOT mint an item, only make a match the guard already found stricter.** 🔑 **THE TWO ENDS ARE ASYMMETRIC BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REASONING, and my own reachability sweep caught it: a first draft excluded `-` on BOTH sides and reddened its own ordinary-markup control, because a hyphen-adjacent mention of a genuinely carried id then reads ABSENT — a FALSE RED on ordinary desk prose, which is how a guard gets excused into uselessness (F-1460-1). LEADING excludes alphanumerics only (an id always starts `F-`, so the only real hazard is being the tail of a longer word); TRAILING excludes the hyphen too, and that half IS load-bearing, since ids are multi-segment and `F-MILK-3` is a strict prefix of the equally valid `F-MILK-3-SS-4`.** ✅ **BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL BEFORE LANDING (F-1274-2): exactly ONE real BACKLOG row key changes across 1988 rows — `F-GNT-4` → `F-GNT-4b`, a real sub-id now keying itself — and ZERO verdicts move on the qualifying set. Legacy desk suites 86/86.** 🔒 `scripts/desk-birth-prefix-token-guard.test.mjs` — 17 arms, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (battery GREEN, **401** node tests / 0 fail, 20 legs, up from 384). 🔬 **TEETH, every variant manufactured on a staged copy whose patch ASSERTS ITS EDIT MATCHED (s2221): pre-cure reds 5 of 9 behaviours · the REFUTED ledger-anchored grammar reds 3 · key-only and not-owed-only partial cures each red exactly the arms built for them · leading-hyphen reds the markup arm ALONE · trailing-loose reds the multi-segment arm ALONE.** ⚠️ **THE REFUTED CURE IS WORSE THAN s2229 RECORDED, measured here rather than inherited: the ledger-anchored form does not key the PARENT, it keys NOTHING — the trailing `\b` fails against the sub-id letter and `\d+` cannot backtrack past it, so `rowId` returns null and `analyse` drops the row before it is ever asked about. 🟡 **F-2230-2 (s2230 2026-08-23, A NEGATIVE RESULT BANKED WITH ITS MECHANISM SO THE NEXT FIRE INHERITS A REASON AND NOT A VERDICT — THE CARRYFORWARD HALF OF s2229'S AIM IS SOUND, AND THE AIMING RULE THAT SPLIT IT)** — F-2214-1's rule: a negative result is a measurement and inherits a measurement's duties. **`desk-carryforward-guard`'s unanchored `FINDING` is NOT a defect, and the mechanism is what matters rather than the verdict: it parses BOTH desks with the SAME predicate and compares them with an exact array `.includes`, so a truncating key truncates IDENTICALLY on both sides and cancels. 🟢 **F-2227-1 (s2227 2026-08-23, FOUND AND CURED THE SAME FIRE ON A DRY BOARD — THE TWENTY-FOURTH CONSECUTIVE FIRE TO EXECUTE ITS PREDECESSOR’S AIM RATHER THAN ADMIRE IT): `desk-state-audit.mjs` JUDGED LINE-1 BY A RETIRED CONVENTION, SO ITS DOCUMENTED `SKIP` HAD SILENTLY BECOME AN rc=2 REFUSAL THAT ACCUSES THE WRONG SUBJECT.** The lock test at `:42` was `line1.startsWith('ACTIVE')`. 🔧 **[F-2238-1] — THE ASSAY WORKER WILL NOT BOOT ON THE PRODUCTION BOX WITHOUT `ASSAY_BUILD_ID`, AND THE REQUIREMENT LIVED ONLY IN A RUN LOG (found + CURED in the s2238 drain).** `assay-worker.mjs` resolves its id as `ASSAY_BUILD_ID?.trim() || execFileSync('git',['rev-parse','--short','HEAD'])`, at module top level, uncaught. `||` short-circuits so the git call never runs when the var is set — but unset, it throws on any box without a checkout. **That box is live**: `docs/ops/agenttown-server.md` states the deploy recipe verbatim as rsync with `--exclude .git` (*"no git on the box"*) and `goldrush-assay` is systemd, so the failure mode is a silent restart loop on the next engine update, not a visible error. The runner FOUND this in its own review and supplied the escape hatch correctly — it then wrote *"Production must set it when rsyncing the worker"* into `tasks/runs/…c6-tape-build-id.md.log`, **a surface nobody reads at deploy time.** ⚖️ Non-blocking for the merge: the git fallback is correct everywhere a checkout exists (dev, CI, every test), so this is an OPS precondition, not a code defect — cured in the drain commit by landing it in the runbook's worker env list AND its DEPLOY/UPDATE recipe, where a deployer actually stands, with the stale-value hazard named (a wrong id is worse than none: it declares skew against tapes the assayer itself could verify). 💡 **This is §1.1's own reusable half in operational dress — *a cure parked outside the tracked law is a cure the factory does not have*. The fix was known, correct, and one surface short.**

🔬 **F-2128-1 (s2128 2026-08-21 — A FIRE'S PLAIN `git commit` SWEEPS A CONCURRENT WRITER'S STAGED INDEX, AND CAN CONCLUDE THEIR IN-PROGRESS MERGE. MEASURED TWICE IN ONE FIRE, ON MYSELF.)**
⚠️ **PATH-SCOPED `git add` DOES NOT PROTECT YOU, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** The standing law is *"path-scoped `git add` only, NEVER `-A`"* and I obeyed it exactly, both times. **`git add` scoping controls what YOU add; `git commit` commits the INDEX — and on a multi-writer main the index is not yours.** Instance 1: `git add <4 paths>` then a bare `git commit` produced **a MERGE COMMIT** — `b2c35f2d5`, whose `%P` carries TWO parents (`36c74635a` my own lock commit, and `5bc4650cf` the attended session's branch tip) and whose diff is **44 files**. My commit *concluded the attended session's in-progress e3-fairground merge* and stamped it with my authoring headline. Instance 2, seven minutes later and after I already knew: `git add <1 path>` then a bare `git commit` → `433cea13d` swept three more staged files (`assets/contracts/null-floors.json`, `docs/bench/same-game-audit.md`, `scripts/same-game-audit.test.mjs`).
✅ **OUTCOME BENIGN, AND VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — BUT DO NOT READ THAT AS "THE WINDOW IS SAFE".** The swept content was **decided and gated**, not undecided: `reviews/e3-fairground-crowd-flocks.md` line 3 carries **`Verdict: MECHANIC APPROVED · ADMISSION HELD`** (attended gate, 2026-08-20). I then checked the tree I had produced, because concluding a merge makes it mine: **`npx tsc --noEmit` clean · no conflict markers in tracked `src`/`scripts`/`e2e`/`assets` · their three authored files present** (`src/systems/CrowdFlockSystem.ts`, `src/entities/CrowdFlock.ts`, `e2e/e3-fairground-flocks.spec.ts`). **Nothing was lost and nothing undecided shipped. The damage is ATTRIBUTION:** merge `b2c35f2d5` is headlined *"the stdin-rejection deadlock"* while its content is the fairground admission — and a commit headline names intent, so this one names the wrong intent (the `a-commit-headline-names-intent-only-stat-names-content` shape). **Had that merge been UNDECIDED, I would have shipped it past its own verdict** — which is exactly the exposure F-1589-5 records, and it was luck, not design, that it was already approved.
🪞 **THE REUSABLE HALF: THIS IS F-1589-5 SEEN FROM THE OTHER SIDE, AND THE PAIR IS ONLY COMPLETE WITH BOTH.** That finding binds the MERGER — *never leave a merge staged on main; merge and commit as ONE act.* This one binds **every other writer**: a plain `git commit` will close somebody else's open window for them, without warning, whatever your own `git add` discipline was. The two laws defend the same window from opposite ends.
➡️ **THE CURE IS ONE CHARACTER-CLASS AND COSTS NOTHING: COMMIT WITH A PATHSPEC — `git commit -m "…" -- <paths>`** — which commits ONLY those paths and leaves everything else staged for its owner, instead of `git add <paths>` followed by a bare `git commit`. ⓘ **NOT rewritten, deliberately:** a live concurrent writer was mid-flight, `git reset` is owner-approval-gated (`safety-and-quality.md`), and `CLAUDE.md` §7.7 forbids the irreversible act — so this is superseded BY RECORD, the house remedy, rather than by rewriting main's history under someone who is still writing to it. **GATE: an attended session may re-headline or re-attribute `b2c35f2d5` if it judges the attribution worth a rewrite; a fire must not.**

['show','--first-parent','-m','--name-only'] : ['show','--name-only']`. **`tk-2026-08-19` (s2076) replaced that with a single unconditional `git show --pretty=format: --name-only` for every commit**, under a header comment reading *"Same shape as artifacts/tk-2026-08-18/classify.mjs"* — an assertion of sameness about a file the author had just rewritten. ⚠️ **WHY THAT IS WRONG AND NOT MERELY DIFFERENT: for a true merge commit `git show --name-only` prints the COMBINED diff, which is empty for any path that matches one parent.** A merge that lands player code therefore reports **zero files** and is filed as *bookkeeping* — the exact bucket a digest uses to say *"no player-visible change landed."* 🕳️ **THE REASON NOBODY SAW IT, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE HALF: `2026-08-19` had 47 commits and `0` merges.** A defect in merge handling cannot manifest on a day with no merges, so the regression's own landing day was the one day in the retained window that could not test it — and the digest it produced (*"zero merges … the county stood still for a day"*) was **correct**, which is worse than a visible red, because a correct output is read as evidence the instrument works. 📊 **PRICED ON FIRST EXPOSURE. `2026-08-20`: 180 first-parent commits, `30` merge commits.** Inherited unchanged the classifier reports **21** player-visible; the correct method reports **28**. **7 merges invisible**, and **4 of them are headlines in the digest I just filed** — `20895457a` **e7-dead-band, an entire new map (+10 player files, read as 0)** · `db3d10076` worn-out machines / alive cap (+6, owner-ruled) · `8086ee597` the season roll (+2) · `9dca85081` the deepwater claim re-admission (+6). The other 3 (`9d902829a`, `fd6b6952c`, `5ca1c00c9`) were dismissals either way, so the damage would have been silent in both directions. ✅ **NO PUBLISHED DIGEST IS FALSE — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, AND I CHECKED BEFORE I ACCUSED.** My first back-check flagged `2026-08-15` as under-reported (legacy 1 → fixed 6) and I did **not** file that: I read `artifacts/tk-2026-08-15/classify.mjs` first and found it carries the merge-safe branch, so its digest's `6 touching src/public/assets` and its five merge headlines were right when written. **The gap was in my control, not in that digest.** Across the whole retained window only `08-15` and `08-20` contain merges touching player paths; `08-18`'s 3 merges genuinely touch none (`fixed = 0`, matching its published `0`); `08-16`/`08-17`/`08-19` have zero merges. **The regression existed for exactly one digest and that digest was unaffected.** 🔧 **THE CURE, AND ITS HONEST LIMIT.** `artifacts/tk-2026-08-20/classify.mjs` lists files as `git diff --name-only <sha>^1 <sha>` — the right question for a `--first-parent` walk (*what did this commit bring onto main relative to its first parent*), correct for merges and identical to `--name-only` for ordinary commits. **CONTROLLED, not asserted: across all 180 of yesterday's commits it agrees with the `08-15`-lineage `show --first-parent -m` method on `180/180`**, so it RESTORES the lineage rather than inventing a third method. It also **computes both methods every run and prints every disagreement**, so the next fire that copies it forward carries the control with it and a future silent revert announces itself in the output. ⚠️ **That defence lives in the artifact that gets copied forward, so it survives exactly as long as the copying does — it is not a guard and I am not claiming it is one.** 🚫 **NO GUARD IS PROPOSED, DELIBERATELY.** These classifiers are per-day retained evidence, not a run surface; a battery test over `artifacts/tk-*/` would red on every historical file the RETENTION LAW forbids editing, and would be excused into uselessness within a week (the `cross-engine` label's fate, F-1460-1). 💡 **THE GENERAL SHAPE, worth more than the instance: a regression that lands on a day containing no instances of the thing it breaks is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION, and its clean output is actively misleading. When a copied-forward instrument is rewritten, the comment claiming continuity is the author's INTENT, never a measurement — diff it against its stated ancestor, and price it against the busiest day it will meet rather than the day it lands on.** ⓘ Also caught by my own pre-commit verifier: a hand-typed hash `c61ed4dc` for `b3ed55bb1` (dropped a `d`), which resolves to nothing — the F-1633-1 wrong-needle class, found because the digest's hashes were checked against `git` rather than re-read. 🟡 **F-2087-3 — `status-archive-audit` CANNOT EVER CLEAR AN ATTENDED-AUTHORED LINE-1, SO ITS RED HERE IS UNFIXABLE BY THE FIRE IT ACCUSES (measured s2087, VERIFIED by reading the predicate).** `sessionOf()` (`scripts/status-archive-audit.mjs:53`) recognises exactly two ownership shapes — `s<N> fire` and `s<N> handoff` — so a line-1 written by an ATTENDED session (`ACTIVE 2026-08-20T15:58Z (attended drain) — …`, no s-number anywhere) resolves to `lostSession === null`. 🔴 **F-2080-3 (s2080 2026-08-20) — A REVIEW CALLED IT "A ONE-PARAM FIX, PROVEN"; THE PARAM IT NAMES WOULD RETURN HTTP 400. F-SR-5 IS A TWO-AXIS MAPPING QUESTION AND IS NOT FIRE-AUTHORABLE.** `reviews/assay-season-roll.md:17` files F-SR-5 as *"(player-visible, one-param fix)"* with the cure already *"proven by the agent's own battery: `?view=byStack&season=1` merges through existing `mergeFieldBooks`"*. Measured at source before authoring anything against it, and the cure does not survive the reading. The reader's `loadSeasonResults(seasonId)` (`src/encyclopedia/reader.ts:538-552`) sets `view` and `epoch` and **never sets `season`** — that half of the finding is TRUE and the page really does read the wrong ledger post-roll. But the value it holds is a **CHRONICLE** id: `SEASONS` (`src/seasons/registry.ts:10-20`) are `founding-season` / `same-game-season`, **strings**, while `parseSeason` (`functions/api/standings.ts:933-938`) accepts only `/^[0-9]{1,4}$/` ∈ `KNOWN_SEASONS = {1,2}` and returns `null` otherwise → `:287` refuses with **400 `bad_season`**. So `url.searchParams.set('season', seasonId)` — the literal one-param fix — **breaks the page instead of fixing it**, and the working version requires deciding that the founding *chronicle window* corresponds to *ledger* season 1. ⚠️ **THAT DECISION IS THE THING THE SOURCE FORBIDS TAKING CASUALLY:** `standings.ts:161-168` says the two axes "are genuinely different and **must never be conflated**", that the chronicle "partitions by WHEN a row was posted; its current window already contains pre-assay rows, **so it cannot express the roll**", and — in the same breath — that season pages were deliberately left alone: *"Untouched here: rows keep their chronicle name and the season pages keep telling the story."* The windows do not align by construction, so no mapping is a mere lookup. ➡️ **THEREFORE F-SR-5 IS ATTENDED/OWNER-GATED, NOT FIRE-AUTHORABLE**, and §2E's hard limit applies verbatim: *needs a design fork → do NOT author*. The cheap-looking fix is the trap. 💡 **THE CLASS, and it is the third time in this one fire that re-verifying an inherited claim overturned it:** a finding's *cure* is a claim exactly as much as its *defect* is, and the two can have opposite truth values — here the defect is real, the cure is wrong, and the word "proven" was carried from a battery that proved something adjacent (that `mergeFieldBooks` merges a season-scoped payload) rather than the fix itself. **A cure inherits its author's confidence, not their evidence — re-derive the lever, never the conclusion.** (Same family as F-1590-1's prove-the-lever rule, arriving from the ledger side rather than the master side.)

🔵 **F-1648-2 (s1648 2026-08-11, CURED IN THE SAME FIRE — THE FACTORY REPORTED `RESUMED` WHILE ITS IMPLEMENT SIDE WAS DEAD, AND IT STAYED DEAD BECAUSE TWO SEPARATE `pgrep -f` CHECKS EACH MATCHED THE COMMAND THAT WAS RUNNING THEM).** The resume one-liner was `until ! pgrep -f "FIRE PROTOCOL"; do sleep 15; done; nohup bash scripts/lane-runner-v3.sh …`, run as one backgrounded shell. **Both of its guards are self-matching, because the whole command line — including its own search strings — is the argv `pgrep -f` searches:** (a) the wait loop matches its own shell forever, so the restart it guards **can never fire**; (b) `lane-runner-v3.sh`'s otherwise-correct stale-lock self-heal — *"if no OTHER runner process exists, the lock is a corpse"* — counted that same wrapper as another runner, declined to clear the corpse lock left by the killed loop, and logged *"another instance running … Remove if stale."* **Net effect: the ops commit says the runner was restarted, `tasks/.runner.lock` was a month-old corpse, and no runner process existed at all.** ⚠️ **The dangerous part is not the outage, it is that the LEDGER SAID OTHERWISE** — Mistake #4's shape at factory scale: a fire reading the resume commit inherits *"runners restarted"* and never probes. ✅ **CURED s1648**: corpse lock cleared, runner started detached with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` **scrubbed from its environment** (a runner started from a fire shell would otherwise inherit the fire's config dir and silently pin every LANE playwright run to `workers: 1` via the `isFireShell` key in `playwright.config.ts` — §3.1's mechanism firing in exactly the direction it is written to forbid), and verified up by pidfile+log rather than by the fact that the command returned. 💡 **GENERAL: `pgrep -f <string>` run from a shell whose own command line contains `<string>` always finds itself. Any liveness probe written inline in the command it is probing for is a tautology** — probe from a script file, or match a pattern the probing command cannot contain.

🔵 **F-1639-1 (s1639 2026-08-10, FOUND AT THE sea-2 DRAIN — NON-BLOCKING, GATED, CURE OUTSIDE THIS SLICE'S FIREWALL): the grouped standings API keeps ONE cell per group×contract, so a second season's page will UNDER-REPORT and its honest-empty line will become a FALSE statement.** The runner reported this itself as *"the grouped API loses cross-season cells"*; I verified it in code rather than taking it. `functions/api/standings.ts:324` guards cell creation with `if (!group.contracts.has(contractId))`, so the first row wins and the cell carries **only that row's** season; `src/encyclopedia/reader.ts` then filters with `cell.season === season` and drops a row whose cells all fall away. **Vacuous today — exactly one season exists, so every cell carries the same label or none.** The day Season 2 opens: a Mind whose best ride on a contract was in Season 1 has no cell for Season 2 and vanishes from its page, and if that empties the page the county says *"No rides were posted for this season"* — **which would be false.** That is the sharp edge, and it is worse than a missing row because it reads as a fact. 🟢 **F-1598-1** (s1598 2026-08-09, CURED THIS FIRE — THE RELEASE GATE RAN `build:release` BARE, SO THE E1-LEAK CHECK NEVER EXECUTED AND THE RELEASE SHIPPED PAST AN `rc=1` TRANSCRIPT). Cured in `ca9297789`. ⚙️ **WHAT WAS WRONG:** the 2026-08-09 RELEASE GATE battery invoked `npm run build:release` through `scripts/gate-battery.mjs` with no `--env`, so the release assertion threw on its `GR_RELEASE=e1` precondition — the leaf that proves no E2–E10 content leaked into the public build **never ran**. The battery recorded `SUMMARY {"tsc":0,"build":0,"build:release":1,"core-e2e":0}` / `OVERALL rc=1`, the deploy proceeded, and the ledger row `263430bfe` called the release *live and verified* — leaving a **red transcript as the release’s only evidence file**. The house form has been written down since F-RB-1: `GR_RELEASE=e1 npm run build:release`; the transcript has no `env+` line, which is the proof it was not used. ✅ **THE RELEASE ITSELF IS SOUND, AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT:** re-running the assertion against the SHIPPED `dist/` returned **1883 files, 111,070,567 bytes, zero later manifest ids or plate/GLB assets, checked against a non-empty 262-stem denominator** (`artifacts/s1598-release-recheck.txt`). ⚠️ **But that is luck, not the gate — a genuine leak would have sailed through the same hole.** 🔧 **CURE AT THE DRIVER, NOT THE CALLER:** a job whose argv names `build:release` or `assert-release-build.mjs` without `GR_RELEASE=e1` in the RESOLVED environment is now **MISUSE → rc=2, nothing measured**, matching the driver’s existing fail-closed handling of a bad `--cwd`/`--env`. 🚫 **DELIBERATELY NOT CURED BY DEFAULTING THE VARIABLE:** that would silently satisfy the precondition the guard exists to enforce, and would break the standing positive control asserting that a bare invocation is still refused. ✅ **PROVED BY MANUFACTURING THE DEFECT** (the s1299/s1300 standard): with the CLI check removed the new refusal test FAILS; cured file restored **byte-identical**, sha256 `769f8c10`; `gate-battery` **17/17**. 🩹 **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE GUARD WAS ITSELF THE WORSE BUG, RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED AWAY:** its refusal arm spawned the REAL `npm run build:release`, which in the pre-fix arm executed for **15.2 s and overwrote the repo’s `dist/`** — the very bytes that had just been deployed and verified. 🟡 **F-1516-2 (s1516 — A DONE-MOVE'S MTIME IS ITS QUEUE-INSERTION TIME, NOT ITS COMPLETION TIME, SO §2B'S OWN DRAIN TRIGGER IS WRONG IN THE STARVING DIRECTION.** Non-blocking, but it can silently cost a whole fire's drain.) `scripts/fire.md` §2B tells a fire to drain *"done-moves in `tasks/done/` newer than the last handoff"*. 📐 **THE MECHANISM, measured on this fire's own dispatch rather than inferred:** the lane runner `mv`s the queue file into `tasks/done/` **at COMPLETION** — but `mv` **preserves the mtime the file acquired when it was `cp`'d into the queue at DISPATCH**. Timeline, three independent clocks: master written **09:32:08** · done-move mtime **09:34:13** (the `cp`) · run-log last write **09:39:27** (the actual completion). So `ls -lt tasks/done/` sorts by **dispatch** order and every done-move's mtime **understates** completion — here by ~5 minutes, and for `f1515-1` by **27**. ⚠️ **THAT GAP IS EXACTLY WHERE A DRAIN GETS SKIPPED, and it nearly happened this fire:** `f1515-1` was queued **09:07**, completed **~09:34**, and its done-move carries mtime **09:07** — **older than s1515's 09:21 handoff**. A fire obeying §2B's sentence literally would have concluded there was nothing newer than the last handoff and **skipped a finished, gated, mergeable slice**; I found it only because I listed `tasks/runs/` and read a log tail. It merged as `25b32142`. 💡 **The trap is that the rule LOOKS self-checking** — a timestamp compared against a timestamp — which is why it survived; nothing about `ls -lt` announces that one of the two clocks belongs to a different event. ⓘ **I first mis-diagnosed this as "the runner done-moves at dispatch"** (which would have meant a done-move proves only that a run STARTED) and wrote that into my handoff before measuring it; the three-clock comparison above refuted my own correction. **A done-move DOES mean the run finished — its mtime just does not say when.** **REC: trigger §2B on the RUN LOG's mtime (which is written at completion) or on `git log main..lane/*` (content, not clocks), and treat `tasks/done/` mtimes as dispatch order only.** Related: [F-1516-1], [F-1300-4].

🟡 **F-1516-1 (s1516 — A PROBE CAN VALIDATE THE RIGHT MECHANISM THROUGH THE WRONG MODULE SYSTEM, AND THE CONJUNCT IT "PROVED" IS THE ONE NOBODY RE-EXAMINES.** Non-blocking; no corrective queued — recorded as a class, and the cure is already named in the row above.) s1516 priced the F-1510-3 successor with deliberate rigour: it asked the [F-1514-1] question **conjunct by conjunct** — *would performing this scope make the gate sentence TRUE?* — and tabled five answers. **Four were right. The fifth was wrong, and it was the one backed by an EXPERIMENT rather than by reading.** 🔬 **THE MECHANISM:** the decisive probe ran in `/tmp/s1516-pw-probe`, a directory with **no `package.json`**, so Playwright transpiled its TypeScript config to **CommonJS**, where `__dirname` exists — and it duly returned a real sha (`e67840916ccc…`, the fire's own lock commit), which read as conclusive. This repo is **`"type": "module"`**, so the identical config loads as **ESM** and `__dirname` is undefined. **The probe matched its subject on flags and on Playwright version, but not on COMPOSITION**, and the pricing doc plus the authored master both went on to *mandate* `__dirname`. Cost: one lane run (92,161 tokens), recovered in full because the master licensed exactly this negative result and named `__dirname` as a candidate failure. ⚠️ **THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is what makes this worth a row:** a conjunct you verified by *reasoning* stays visibly provisional and gets re-read; a conjunct you verified by *running something* acquires the authority of a measurement and is never revisited. **So the audit question is not "did I test it?" but "did my test share the subject's composition?"** — module system, runtime, config loader, and package boundary are all part of a probe's claim, not its scenery. 💡 Same family as [a control arm must match in composition, not just flags] and [a probe that dies in your stub is evidence about your stub], but a distinct and nastier polarity: **this probe did not die and did not mislead by failing — it PASSED, and the pass is what did the damage.** **REC (process, not code): when a probe is built OUTSIDE the subject tree for isolation, state in the pricing which properties of the subject the probe does NOT reproduce, and treat every one of them as unproved.** Isolation and representativeness trade against each other, and the trade should be written down rather than discovered by a runner. 🟢 **F-1397-3 (s1397, MEASURED) — `citation-title-guard`'s quote extraction desynchronises on short inline-code spans, so a correct citation can red for reasons in the prose beside it.** Its `QUOTED` regex treats every backtick, straight quote **and apostrophe** as a delimiter and requires 12–160 characters between a pair, so **an unpaired quote character shifts the pairing for everything after it**. Two triggers were measured, both in ordinary prose: an inline-code span shorter than 12 characters (skipped as an opener), and — caught only when this very row first reddened the guard — **a possessive apostrophe, as in "E1's", which is an unpaired delimiter the writer never thinks of as one.** In both cases — the regex then captures the prose *between* code spans instead of the spans themselves. Measured: a verbatim quote of a real source line sat inside the window and was never extracted, because a nearby 9-character span had offset the pairing. Two neighbours worth knowing: the window is ±400 characters, so a citation's verdict can depend on where that window happens to start; and `MIN_PREFIX` is 20, so a 19-character quoted prefix fails. **NOT filed as a defect to fix** — the guard's purpose (recoverability) is served and loosening the regex risks false greens. **Recorded as a cure for the next reader:** put the quote immediately after the citation, in double quotes, with no inline-code spans between them. **GATE: none — informational.**

🟡 **F-1390-2 (s1390 — A COLD vite DEP CACHE INFLATES WHICHEVER ARM RUNS FIRST; MY OWN FIRST RUN WAS A FALSE GREEN.)** Measuring p95 in a freshly-created worktree is unreliable, and it fails in the direction that is hardest to notice: it makes a red gate look **green**. 📊 **Measured on itself, same tree, same machine, 7 minutes apart:** run 1 in a brand-new detached worktree with its own `vite` server → painted **33.9** ms, terrain3d 25.1, ratio **0.74**, test **PASSED in 1.4 m**. Run 2, same commit, stock playwright-managed `npm run dev` and a now-warm dep cache → painted **11.0** ms, terrain3d 16.9, ratio **1.54**, test **FAILED in 19.5 s**. **The whole test got 4× faster on the second run**, which is the tell: vite`s dependency pre-bundling (`Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed`, logged at server start) taxes the early boots, and this spec measures the PAINTED arm first in every contract. The tax therefore lands mostly on the denominator and drags the ratio down under the bar. ⚠️ **I nearly reported that green as a refutation of the predecessor finding** — a fire before me had a red, I had a green on the same tree, and the tempting story was "not reproducible". It was reproducible; my instrument was cold. ➡️ **Rule for any future p95/perf measurement: discard the first run against a newly-created worktree or a newly-started dev server, or warm it with a throwaway run first.** A cheap tell is wall-clock — if the run takes multiples of its usual time, the numbers in it are not comparable to anything. ⓘ The bisect that produced the predecessor row was run AFTER the cache was warm and re-used one server generation throughout, and its boundary was confirmed by two independent passes, so it is not affected. 💡 **The class: a warm-up artefact does not add noise, it adds BIAS — and bias that flatters your hypothesis is the kind you stop looking for.**


**Owed: a bisect for the main commit that crossed the bar.** Not fire-authorable as a fix (it is a perf regression of unknown origin, and the standing order forbids hand-editing the inventory), but the bisect itself is cheap and mechanical. 💡 The class: *"measured under load"* is a reason to withhold a verdict, not a prediction of which way the verdict will go — s1387 and s1388 both leaned toward "probably the shell", and the shell was innocent.

🟢 **F-1370-1 (s1370, MEASURED — NEGATIVE RESULT ACROSS THE FULL DENOMINATOR: NOT ONE OF THE 507 CLOSED GOAL LEAVES RESTS ON A PREMISE THAT LATER CHANGED — AND I REFUTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS THREE TIMES GETTING THERE.)** 🧭 **THE PROBE, AND WHY IT WAS GENUINELY UNRUN.** s1368 §L(3) and s1369 §K(4) both named it and neither ran it: *“nobody has checked the ~505 CLOSED goal leaves for one that closed on a premise that later changed.”* s1368 audited the **18 OPEN** leaves, s1369 the **78 desk rows**; the closed set is the third and largest enumeration, and it is the one where a rotted premise is **silent by construction** — a closed leaf is read by nobody and reds nothing. 📐 **METHOD, CHOSEN AGAINST s1369’S LESSON: I DELIBERATELY PREFERRED READING A SMALL SET AT SOURCE OVER CLASSIFYING A LARGE ONE.** Walking `goals.json` with the concat-`subgoals`+`tasks` walker: **523 status-carrying nodes** — which **independently re-confirms s1369’s and s1364’s 523/18 to the unit, by a third instrument**. **`F-1252-1`** genuinely carries an open owner-desk half. 🔌 **INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED ON A ROW WITH A PHYSICAL ARTIFACT, so the verdict does not rest on ledger prose alone:** `F-1270-4`’s ProcessType ask was tested against **the installed launchd plist this fire runs under** — `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.goldrush.fire.plist` contains **no `ProcessType` key**. ✓ Still genuinely owed. 🚫 **RECOMMENDATION — DO NOT MECHANISE THIS, AND THE EVIDENCE IS MY OWN RUN.** A desk-vs-BACKLOG guard is the obvious next move and it would be a mistake: **the classifier was wrong in 4 of 4 passes, and a guard shipped on ANY intermediate version would have fired 2–29 false alarms against a desk that is clean.** The ledger’s definition-row syntax has **32 markers and ≥4 structural shapes** (bare, list-prefixed, struck `~~`, prose-inside-bold); Only the third is owner-side, so on its face this was authorable work sitting on a board called dry. 📐 **MEASURED, AND MY OWN HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED — the other two nouns were ALREADY DONE, and had been for two weeks.** `wiring`: **25 of 27 ledger rows are present as keys in the `src/world/Terrain3dClaimPilot.ts` registry**; the 2 absent (The Last Claim, The River) are excluded by `docs/MAP-CAMPAIGN-LEDGER.md` **own footnote** (Ark-deck class; Charter Press CP-05), not by a gap. `landmarks`: **36 of 36 packs under `assets/pilots/map-rebuild-spike/landmarks/` contain at least one `.glb` — 196 files, ZERO empty.** ⚠️ **THE DEFECT IS THE DOCUMENT, AND IT FAILS IN THE RARE DIRECTION — IT UNDERSTATES.** `docs/MAP-CAMPAIGN-LEDGER.md` had not been touched since **2026-07-18** (mtime + `git log`), and **8 of its 27 `wired` rows were false, ALL EIGHT understating**: five read `BLOCKED` (The Picnic, Echo Canyon, The Dead Band, Relay Rush, Low Orbit) and three read `—` (The Trestle, Blackout Ridge, The Fairground); **every one of the eight is wired.** Its `sculpt` column read `—` for all 27 while **32 terrain sculpts sat on main**. 🎯 **WHY THAT COSTS SOMETHING, WHICH IS THE WHOLE FINDING: this is the file the owner opens to know what to test.** Its header is his own bargain, verbatim — *"the last column is yours — verdict in one word, I file the rest"* — and all 27 `OWNER VERDICT` cells are `—`. **A ledger reporting five maps BLOCKED and nothing sculpted tells him the campaign is not ready to test. It has been ready since 2026-07-18.** So the stale document was suppressing the exact owner action that closes the leaf, while the leafs `status:"building"` + absent `blockedReason` kept it invisible to `drain-block-check --all` (which keys strictly on `status==="blocked"`) and to every dry-board sweep. **A 25-item owner ask has therefore never once reached the owner desk in 29 dry fires** — I checked the carried-findings list of each of the last handoffs and it appears in none. ✅ **REFUTED IN PASSING, recorded per s1361 rule that refutations are worth as much as findings — TWO of them.** (1) The five maps whose own `-terrain-contract.json` sits on disk unimported are **not** unwired gaps: each is a **deliberate reuse mount with an intent comment at its call site** (`c19ae56b` *"art: close final five reuse mounts"*), e.g. *"Glow Mesa alias: The Picnic keeps the caprock sculpt and changes campaign rules only."* I nearly filed that as unreachable art (the F-1187 shape) and the call-site comments say otherwise. (2) The Trestle and The Dead Band are absent from all 29 `kind: 'contract'` dispatches in `src/town/worldDispatches.ts` — which looked like a Mistake #10 player-reachability gap until I read `e2e/e2-trestle.spec.ts`, which reaches Trestle by **seeding a Hill Mine win and advancing the epoch contract family**. Different mechanism, not a gap. ➡️ **CURED THIS COMMIT, and the cure is transcription repair toward MEASURED FACT, not a new decision (F-1364-1 precedent — no owner action is consumed and this needs no ruling):** the ledger table is rebuilt from main with a `landmarks` column added, each of the 7 reuse mounts named with its source and its call-site quote, a DO-NOT-"FIX"-THE-REUSE-MOUNTS warning, and a dated re-measurement banner stating what was wrong. **The `OWNER VERDICT` column was NOT touched — it is his, and filling it would be the one move guaranteed to be wrong.** The goal leaf carries the same correction plus an explicit DO-NOT-AUTHOR (there is nothing left to wire). **`status` left at `"building"`: a fire may not set a leaf blocked.** 💡 *Reusable shape: **we are well defended against documents that over-claim and blind to documents that under-claim.** Every law here — Mistake #1, #13, #16, the shipped-ness tests, the drain gates — exists to stop a false DONE, because a false DONE ships a defect. A false NOT-DONE ships nothing, so nothing reds, no gate fires, and the cost is invisible: it is simply an action that never gets asked for. **The tell is a leaf whose remaining-work list has more nouns than its blocker list** — that gap is where a finished noun goes to hide. And the reason it survived 29 sweeps is that every one of them asked "what is blocking us?" and the honest answer was "the owner" — which was TRUE, and which is exactly why nobody asked the next question: **blocked on him for WHICH act, and does he know?***

WHEN ONE FILE HOLDS BOTH A MEASUREMENT AND A CONCLUSION, THE CONCLUSION INHERITS THE MEASUREMENT'S AUTHORITY WITHOUT INHERITING ITS SCOPE.** `hero-credit-log.json` earned trust by being right about hero to the second — and spent it on `stoppedBeforeNextCharacter: true`, a claim about a character its instrument never observed. **That is why the sentence survived s1350 quoting this exact file, s1366 reading it and flagging the anomaly, and sixteen fires in between:** everything verifiable around it checks out. ➡️ **The rule I'd hand forward: when a document reports a number and then draws a conclusion, ask what the instrument's DENOMINATOR was, and whether the conclusion stays inside it. 🟡 **F-1366-1 (s1366, MEASURED + ACTED — "REGENERABLE" WAS DOING THREE DIFFERENT JOBS IN ONE WORD, AND THE 5% IT WAS WRONG ABOUT IS THE CURATED LAYER.)** I did not re-measure F-1331-4's byte count (it re-derived exactly: **602 files / 556.81 MB**). And the run's real product was a **choice** — RUN-NOTE's *"Best-of-three selections"* table (3 sets × 4 directions, picked by lowest first-to-last RMSE across 36 takes, seam RMSE 0.0162–0.1724). **That table is now safe in git; the takes it indexes are not.** Kill the pixels and the surviving record indexes frames that no longer exist, and the QA verdict beside it (identity **PASS**, pinned-gear **FAIL**, chroma **FAIL**) describes images nobody can look at. ⚠️ **(3) BYTE-LEVEL, CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BECAUSE THIS AUDIT HAS SHIPPED A FALSE ZERO TWICE (F-1054-1/F-1055-1): the whole `pose-library` is untracked while its siblings are tracked.** `git ls-files assets/motion-pilot` = **2362** tracked files; `git ls-files assets/motion-pilot/pose-library` = **0**. All three sheets RUN-NOTE names as *Deliverables* hash to blobs in **no object database** (`743a6fb3`, `01e2c33f`, `f4a5f630`) and **differ from every git copy**; **`char-hero-sheet-idle8.png` has no copy on main under any name** — its only git variant (`68704920`, different bytes) sits on `origin/save/art-staging-20260725` at `f23c7516`. ✅ **ACTED — THE s1350 SHAPE RECURS EXACTLY ONE LEVEL DOWN, SO THE CURE IS THE SAME SHAPE.** Decomposed the hole by ROLE, not by type: **94.81% is per-take intermediate** (frames **335.78 MB**/480 · video takes **82.90 MB**/49 · takes123 sheets **70.75 MB**/25 · per-take stills **38.46 MB**/28) — that genuinely *is* the repo-weight question. **5.19% is the CURATED layer: 20 files / 28.92 MB** — the 3 Deliverable sheets, the **12 best-of-three picks (3×4 — exactly the selection table)**, and the 5 four-view composites. Salvaged to **`save/art-staging-20260801` `ca534290`** (parent `781079ed`, s1350's own branch), by `commit-tree` against a **temp index** so main's working tree and index were never touched (**§3.0b custody**, `git status` verified after). **Pushed and verified BY ASKING ORIGIN, not by push's exit code** — `git ls-remote` returns `ca534290…`, and the three deliverable blobs were **read back from `FETCH_HEAD`** at the same hashes. 📉 **NET: AT RISK 602 files / 556.81 MB → 582 files / 527.89 MB; LOCAL-ONLY 0; SALVAGED 152 → 172.** ⚖️ **F-1331-4 IS NOT CLOSED AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-EMPTED** — the **528 files / 527.89 MB** of per-take intermediates it asks a ruling on are untouched, and that ruling is still purely about repo weight. **What changed is that the ruling can now be taken calmly on its merits**, because the layer that encodes a decision no longer dies with the disk. ↩️ **VETO WINDOW (§7.4): this is a fire's judgement call inside a directory the owner has a pending ruling on**, taken on s1350's explicit precedent and on the RETENTION LAW's owner-verbatim *"we live with our memories"*. It adds 28.92 MB to a `save/` branch that is **never merged to main**, so it cannot change the weight being ruled on. **Reverse with one word — one ref delete.** 💡 **REUSABLE SHAPE, AND IT IS THE SHARPER HALF: a classifier's CATEGORIES are an argument, and they get inherited as fact.** s1350's instrument split the hole by **file extension** — `RECIPE = .json/.mjs/.md`, everything else `OUTPUT (png/mp4 — regenerable)` — and that binary is stated as a comment in `s1350-recipe.mjs` itself. It was right that recipe ≠ output; it was wrong that **output is uniform**. Within one extension sat takes *and* the picks among them, and the picks are irreplaceable for a reason no extension can see: **they are not data, they are a decision about data.** ➡️ **The rule I'd hand forward: when you inherit a classification, do not just re-check which bucket things fell into — ask what question the buckets were built to answer, and whether it is the question you now need answered.** A taxonomy built to find "what can't be regenerated?" cannot find "what wouldn't be the same if it were", and *the second question is the one that matters for anything a human chose.*

🟢 **F-1365-1 (s1365, MEASURED — NEGATIVE RESULT, THREAD CLOSED: THE CLOSED-LEAF HALF OF THE LOSSY-TITLE CLASS IS CLEAN, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL.)** Ran the probe s1364 named as UNRUN (its §K(3)): it had diffed the **18 OPEN** leaf titles against their source rulings and explicitly flagged the **480 closed** (`431 merged` + `49 shipped`) as never checked, guessing the hazard there was *"probably milder — nobody seeks permission from a closed leaf"*. ⚠️ **I tested a sharper version of that guess, because on a board DRY for 26 consecutive fires the expensive closed-leaf failure is not a false permission but a FALSE COMPLETION — a title claiming totality is exactly what would keep a board falsely dry.** 📐 **STRATIFIED, not swept** (s1364 said sample, do not walk 480): 480 closed → **164** whose title carries a claim-word → **20** asserting TOTALITY over an enumerable set → the ones decidable against artefacts on disk. ✅ **RESULT: NO DEFECT FOUND, and every check refuted the hypothesis for a reason worth keeping.** **(1) The denominator DID move and the factory caught it:** two leaves claim *"all 41"* (`plates-028-031`, `board-card-images`) and the contract set is now **42** — `e1-drill-yard` arrived with PC-01. 🟡 **F-1346-1 (s1346, MEASURED — s1345 §H(3) ASKED FOR A PROBE FOR ROWS WHOSE SUBJECT IS A *DOCUMENT*; IT IS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST RESULT IS THAT MOST OPEN ROWS ARE NOT PROBEABLE AT ALL).** s1345 cleared the five cheapest CODE-subject rows with `git log` plus a read, then named the gap: the remainder argue about a guard's source, a law surface, an inventory or a master, and *"those need a different probe than `git log`, and nobody has designed one."* ✓ **BUILT: `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs`.** These rows are unusually quotable — they cite a path and then quote the exact sentence they are arguing about — so the probe asks one question per quote: **does that verbatim string still occur in a file the row names?** Proximity to a path citation decides *whether* a quote is checkable; the union of every path the row names decides the *verdict* (both halves were measured necessary — see F-1346-2). 📊 **LIVE RESULT, and the headline is the denominator, not the hit rate: of 61 open rows, 28 offer NOTHING checkable and only 41 quotes across 33 rows can be asked at all.** Of those 41, **15 present / 26 gone**; rows rank ABSENT 20 / PRESENT 13 / UNRESOLVED 28. ⚠️ **ABSENT RANKS A ROW FOR PROBING — IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND NOT A DEFECT**, and I am naming the three false-positive classes I measured rather than leaving them for the next reader to rediscover: a quoted line later **EXTENDED** (F-1336-2 — `AP-08 — THE ALPHA EXCHANGE + THE COUNTY FAIR` is alive and well in the spec; a `; lineage: …` was appended after the row quoted it), a **shell command** quoted as evidence (F-1336-3), and a quote of **another ROW** rather than a file. ⚖️ **AND ABSENCE HAS NO DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE LIMIT THAT MATTERS:** a row may quote text asserting what IS in a file (gone ⇒ premise rotted) or the text it says is MISSING and ought to be added (gone ⇒ the row is still LIVE). F-1284-1 is the second kind — `"Bash(bash scripts/deploy.sh)"` is genuinely absent from the settings file, and that absence is the finding, not its expiry. **A verdict still requires reading the row.** ⓘ Also worth the next fire's minute: a row is flagged if **any one** of its quotes is gone, so output is sorted by the FRACTION gone — **F-1305-1 and F-1345-1 both flag ABSENT while the sentence each is actually arguing about is still in place** (I grepped both). **GATE: none — the instrument is committed and self-tested. Its output is a triage ORDER for a future fire, and must not be used to strike a row without reading it.**

🟡 **F-1346-2 (s1346, PROVEN ON MYSELF — MY OWN INSTRUMENT'S SELF-TEST PASSED ON A BUILD THAT WAS ABOUT TO PUBLISH A SPECTACULAR FALSE HEADLINE, BECAUSE CONTROLS MEASURE THE SPECIFICATION AND NOT THE INTENT).** The first build of `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs` reported **ABSENT 41 / PRESENT 1** on the live ledger — i.e. *"almost every open row's premise has vanished"*, which would have been the best paragraph in this handoff and was **entirely false**. ✓ **ROOT CAUSE:** a code-span regex matched the prose sitting **BETWEEN two adjacent backtick spans**, so ordinary ledger narration was harvested as "quotes" attributed to files that never contained it. Tokenising by alternation (odd segments of a split on the delimiter) is the only correct read; the regex is now impossible to reintroduce silently because a **regression control for exactly that string shape** sits in the self-test. 🔁 **THEN IT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME, DIFFERENTLY:** the fix scored each quote against its **nearest** path citation, which looked more precise and was measurably worse — F-1294-1 quotes a sentence that genuinely lives in `scripts/fire.md`, but its nearest citation was `playwright.config.ts`, so an **intact premise was called GONE**. Cure: proximity decides whether a quote is checkable, the union of all named paths decides the verdict. 🪞 **THE PART WORTH INHERITING: the self-test PASSED on the first build, and on the second.** Six controls, all green, all correct — they proved the code did what I had specified, and the specification was the thing that was wrong. **Every one of the three defects was caught the same way instead: by taking a handful of the live verdicts and checking them by hand against the real files** (`grep -c` on the spec, the inventory, the guard header). ➡️ **The rule: a green self-test licenses you to trust the mechanism, never the measurement. 🟡 **F-1345-1 (s1345, MEASURED — `law-pointer-guard` WAS BUILT BECAUSE OF A POINTER THAT LIVES OUTSIDE ITS OWN DENOMINATOR, SO THAT POINTER ROTTED A THIRD TIME WHILE THE GUARD REPORTED PASS EVERY FIRE).** `scripts/law-pointer-guard.mjs` opens by naming its motivating incident (`:5-11`): *"CLAUDE.md §4.10b told the next session to go LOOK at `lane-runner-v3.sh:118` … The same fire found the sweep pointer **`v3:116` rotted to :137**"*. ✓ **But its `SURFACES` list (`:68-75`) is six markdown files** — `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/fire.md`, and the three `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` — **plus `goals.json` `blockedReason` and `drain-block-check.mjs`. ✅ **F-1298-2 (s1298) STRUCK s1345 — CURED IN CODE 2026-07-31 by `088a9138`, AND ITS ROW HAD READ "GATE: none. Fire-authorable, one function" EVER SINCE.** The row described a real race in `env/goldrush-verifiers/goldrush/__init__.py` `_read_sim_reply`: stdout EOFs empty while `stderr_task` is still pending, control reaches `await process.stderr.read()` with a coroutine already waiting on that `StreamReader`, asyncio raises `RuntimeError: read() called while another coroutine is already waiting for incoming data`, the operator loses the diagnostic, and the pending task is destroyed. ✓ **VERIFIED CURED BY MY OWN READ of `:191-213` (not a subagent's word):** `:202-203` cancel **both** tasks and `:204-206` **`await` both** before `:211`'s `stderr.read()`, with `:207` guarding on `stderr_task.cancelled()`. The `await` is the load-bearing half — a bare `.cancel()` only schedules the throw, and `StreamReader._wait_for_data` clears `self._waiter` in a `finally` that does not run until the task is stepped. A discriminating test exists at `env/goldrush-verifiers/tests/test_goldrush.py:70-83` (`test_crashed_sim_preserves_multiline_stderr` closes fd 1 immediately and writes stderr 50 ms later — precisely the finding's shape). ⚠️ **THIRD SPECIMEN OF F-1344-2, and the sharpest yet, because this row was the most ACTIONABLE thing on the board:** it carried an explicit **`GATE: none. Only two commits have ever touched that file. **An idle fire following the ledger's own most inviting row would have spent a lane re-fixing shipped work — the exact harm `findings-state-guard`'s header names, arriving by the exact route it cannot see.**


🟡 **F-1345-2 (s1345, RAISED BY CODE READ — NOT MEASURED BY EXECUTION, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT).** Surfaced while verifying F-1298-2's cure. `env/goldrush-verifiers/goldrush/__init__.py:196` reads `if stdout_task.done() and stdout_task.result():` — and `.result()` **re-raises**. `StreamReader.readline` raises `ValueError` when a line exceeds the stream limit, and the sim is spawned at `:72-83` with **no `limit=`** (✓ verified by my own read of the spawn site), so asyncio's default **64 KiB** applies. A view JSON line over 64 KiB therefore propagates `ValueError` out of `:196` with `stderr_task` **still pending and never cancelled** → *"Task was destroyed but it is pending!"*. ⚖️ **DELIBERATELY NOT FILED AS A RE-OPENING OF F-1298-2:** it is the same *class* (an exit path that skips the cancel-and-await) but a different trigger, and unlike F-1298-2 it produces **no** `RuntimeError` — nothing downstream calls `stderr.read()` on this path. ⚠️ **Severity honestly unknown: I did NOT measure whether any real view line approaches 64 KiB**, and I could not run pytest (the bash gate refused every Python invocation this fire). Same code, same gate, opposite rulings, 4.2× apart. **An unqualified "measure it" gate gets answered by the cheapest harness, and the cheapest harness is idle — the one condition guaranteed NOT to exercise the input the finding is about.** 🔒 **BOTH growth vectors were then bounded, so 12.66 KiB is close to a real ceiling, not a sample:** **(i) `orders` is hard-capped** — `src/agent/StandingOrders.ts` `validateStandingOrders` rejects with *"orders may contain at most 32 entries."* (measured: a 200-order payload is refused), and `validateOrder` byte-bounds every entry via `exactKeys` + closed enums + numeric ranges, leaving **exactly one string field in the whole schema**: HARVEST's `seam`, `length <= 80`. ⚠️ **The orders array is echoed TWICE per view** — `now.orders` *and* `stablePrefix.orders`, 5,139 B each — **together 80.4% of the largest view**, so the dominant term in the payload is the agent's own input, duplicated. **(ii) `appendLog` is the genuinely unbounded one and it is slow:** `src/agent/View.ts` pushes one `waveEntry` per wave with **no truncation** and emits the whole array every view, measured at **~114–121 B/wave** (clean linear: w2:1, w3:2, w4:3 entries) — but real contracts **terminate at wave 2–4**, so reaching 64 KiB from the driven ceiling needs **~450 more waves than any contract produces**. ⚖️ **HONEST VERDICT: the `ValueError` is unreachable today** — but at 19.8% of the limit the margin is one schema change wide (a raised order cap, or a per-wave field, eats it), which is exactly why the gate's order-of-magnitude test is the right one and why it now says cure. ⛔ **WHY A FIRE CANNOT FINISH IT, AND THIS SHARPENS s1351's CANDIDATE NOTE RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT:** F-1351-1 banked this row as candidate (2) reasoning *"the bash gate refused every Python invocation ... does not apply — the emitter is node."* **That was correct, and it is why the measurement finally happened** — but the row Eight saturated children cannot be absent from a CPU-sorted list. **The children had already exited: a timing failure, not a filter failure.** ⚠️ **SCOPE — THIS NARROWS s1273's §E2, WHICH SAID LEAVING IT BROKEN "POISONS AN OWNER-GATED DECISION".** It does not. It is a latency test wearing a behaviour test's clothes. ⚠️ **AND THE DOMINANT TERM IS THE CLICK, NOT THE WAIT:** under load the window decomposes as **click round-trip 284–347 ms**, poll-to-false 8–163 ms, final sample 4–36 ms. **The click alone blows the budget** — which is exactly why F-1262-4's control found the *unmodified* `waitForTimeout(50)` spec failing identically. **No choice of what to wait for — sleep, poll, or state — can fix this**, because the newsie starts walking home the instant the click lands in the page and the test cannot observe anything until the round-trip returns. **The window has to move inside the page.** ➡️ **CORRECTIVE AUTHORED THIS FIRE:** `tasks/lane-b-gazette-welcome-drift-observation-frame.md`, leaf `gazette-welcome-drift-observation-frame` (queued lane-b).

🔻 **F-1263-2 (s1263, MEASURED — I WAS SENT TO IMPLEMENT A RECOMMENDATION AND THE MEASUREMENT REFUTED ITS UNIT; A FINDING'S RECOMMENDATION IS AN UNTESTED SECOND HYPOTHESIS).** F-1262-4 named the corrective precisely: *"sample the newsie over a FIXED FRAME COUNT after `welcomeFollowsPlayer` goes false and assert on that peak."* Its symptom and its diagnosis both hold. ✗ **Its UNIT does not.** Displacement tracks **simulation time**, not frames: `delta` is clamped to `MAX_PRESENTATION_DELTA_SECONDS = 0.05` (`src/core/Loop.ts:27`) and `TownScene.ts:306` builds its `Loop` **with no options**, so a frame is worth anywhere from ~8 ms to 50 ms of sim — a **6× spread in distance per frame** on the same nominal window. ✓ **Measured across both arms**: a 12-frame window reads 0.689–0.766, but a **16-frame window already reads 1.010 under load** — i.e. the recommended instrument breaches the very bound it was proposed to defend, at a frame count a reasonable implementer might have picked. ⓘ **Why the predecessor could not see it:** its scope-1 probe sampled 12 frames on a quiet box and got 0.702, comfortably inside the bound — **the same measurement that made the recommendation look safe is the one that was blind to the variable.** ➡️ **THE FIX IS THE UNIT, AND IT CONVERTS A SAMPLE INTO A GUARANTEE:** bound the window by the town's own `elapsed` (already public on `TownDiagnostics`, `TownScene.ts:155`) rather than by frames. A 0.08 s sim-time window overshoots by at most one clamped delta, so the peak is at most `7 × (0.08 + 0.05) = 0.91 < 1` **on any machine at any load** — a control-flow guarantee rather than a measured hope (the F-1119-1 shape: prefer a guarantee to a number). My helper — the house idiom, `execFileSync('git',['grep',...],{encoding:'utf8'})` wrapped in `try/catch` returning `'(no hits)'` — reported **zero hits for three separate patterns**, and I wrote the words "zero prior record anywhere in the repo". ✓ **All three were false.** Re-run with `maxBuffer: 64*1024*1024`: `Couldn't load texture` → **23 hits**, `GLTFLoader: Couldn` → **23 hits**, `later flagship URLs decline` → **18 hits**. 🔑 **THE MECHANISM, PROVED NOT GUESSED:** `execFileSync` defaults to **1 MB** of captured stdout; a whole-repo `git grep` on this repo now exceeds that, so node kills the child and throws — measured exactly: **`code=ENOBUFS status=null signal=SIGTERM`, `stdout` truncated at 1,113,297 bytes.** ⚠️ **`status` is `null`, NOT 1.** A catch-all cannot tell "the pattern matched nothing" (`rc=1`) from "the output was too big to hold" (`rc=null`), and the house idiom maps **both** to absence. So the failure mode is not a missing match — it is a **DOES-NOT-EXIST claim minted by a buffer ceiling**, which is precisely what `~/.claude/rules/claim-verification.md` forbids and what "*a probe that executes nothing reports zero*" names. 💥 **THE NEAR-MISS IS THE POINT:** on that false negative I was one step from authoring a "new" defect that is **already recorded twice** — as **F-1180-2** (`tasks/BACKLOG.md:76`, the load-sensitive `THREE.GLTFLoader: Couldn't load texture blob:…` transient) and as a measurement in **`logs/suite-red-inventory.md:611`**. F-1180-2's own text predicts this: *"the next full-suite comparison will read it as a NEW red and mis-attribute it."* It nearly did, one fire later, to me. 🟢 **SCOPED HONESTLY — THE COMMITTED SCRIPTS ARE CLEAN, so this is a PRACTICE defect and I deliberately did NOT ship a guard for a subject that does not exist.** Measured across `scripts/**`: 48 files make child-process calls, **13 pass `maxBuffer`, 35 do not** — but **none** carries the catch→empty pattern that converts an error into absence, and the one that would matter most is safe by construction: **`scripts/drain-block-check.mjs`, the §3.0 first-command-of-every-drain guard, captures nothing** (both calls use `stdio:'ignore'`, lines 52–53) and its `catch` correctly wraps a boolean ancestry probe. A node guard aimed at repo scripts would be an unwired guard pointed at a clean subject. ➡️ **The durable fix is the law, not a script: any whole-repo `git grep` driven from `node -e` MUST pass a large `maxBuffer` AND treat `status===1` as the only "no matches" — every other throw is an UNKNOWN, never an absence.** Recorded to memory as the fire-facing rule. **No owner action; nothing owed.**

Fire-authorable, one function** — cancel-and-await `stderr_task` on every exit path, or read the remainder from the completed task rather than re-reading the stream.

⚡ **"GUARDS 8/8" IS A COIN FLIP WHENEVER A LANE IS RUNNING — `test:power-budget` reds 20–33% of the time on a working box, and the distribution says it is PREEMPTION, not a regression (F-1160-2, s1160 2026-07-28, MEASURED n=20 — small fire-authorable corrective, not an owner call).** ✓ Not a flake dismissal and not inherited: s1160 ran the full battery twice in four minutes and got **8/8 then 7/8 then 8/8**, which is worth nothing on its own — so it measured the RATE. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-power-graph-budget.mjs`, **n=20 back-to-back: 4 over cap (20%)**; an independent n=12 earlier in the same fire gave **4 fail (33%)**. 🔑 **The distribution is BIMODAL with a clean gap, which is the whole diagnosis:** sixteen runs cluster **0.368–0.496 ms** (median **0.416**, ~17% under the 0.500 ms cap) and then it jumps straight to **0.631 / 0.658 / 0.725 / 0.899** — *nothing between 0.496 and 0.631*. **A cap set too tight produces values straddling it continuously; a scheduler steal produces exactly this gap.** ✓ Cause verified at source, not guessed: `scripts/check-power-graph-budget.mjs:35-43` asserts the **p95 of `diagnostics().lastStepMs`** — a pure wall-clock CPU measurement with no I/O — against `POWER_GRAPH_LIMITS.solveBudgetMs`, taken from **one** run of 160 samples. Box at the time: **loadavg ~6.9–7.6 of 16 cores**, carrying lane-d's 2396-test playwright suite plus two live wrangler dev servers. **So the guard is measuring the factory, not the game.** ⚠️ **WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING:** the battery is the one s1146 proved had been *red for a day while nobody ran it* and s1159 fought back to 8/8 — **a guard that reds at random is how a battery gets trained-out**, and every fire that writes "guards 8/8" in a handoff is reporting a **sample**, not a state (mine included; the claim in s1160's line-1 is annotated accordingly). ➡️ **RECOMMENDATION (a): take the MINIMUM p95 across 3 repeats inside the script.** The minimum is the least-preempted sample, so it measures the code's real cost; a genuine regression lifts the floor and still trips the gate, while scheduler noise — which only ever *adds* time — is removed by construction. Median body 0.416 leaves ~20% headroom, so the cap itself needs no loosening and **must not be loosened** (that would be the F-1156-2 mistake in a new costume). (b) require a quiet box — rejected: unenforceable, the factory is never quiet by design. **GATE for whoever takes it: re-run the old script n≥20 BEFORE editing (this line is that baseline), then n≥20 after, on a comparably loaded box — the fix is proven by the over-cap count going 4/20 → 0/20 with the median unmoved, not by one green run.** ✅ **RE-DERIVED s1161 BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT — the remedy survives, one third of the diagnosis does not, and the RATE is not a property of the guard.** Per this board’s own law (a finding’s recommendation is an untested second hypothesis), I re-measured rather than authoring the fix off s1160’s numbers. Instrument: `logs/session-scratch/s1161-power-budget-rate.mjs`, two arms **interleaved** (order is a confound), n=12 each, on a box carrying lane-d’s 2396-test suite + two wrangler servers (loadavg **6.91/16**). **(1) THE RATE IS LOAD-DEPENDENT, SO “20%” IS NOT A CONSTANT:** default-QoS came back **1/12 over cap (8%)**, not 20–33%, and the body was far tighter than s1160’s — **0.338–0.371, median 0.346** vs its 0.368–0.496/median 0.416, with a single outlier at **0.529**. Same script, same cap, different hour: the number measures the BOX, not the code. Quote the rate with its load or not at all. **(2) THE “SCHEDULER STEAL” LABEL IS RIGHT IN KIND — and I tried to refute it with a specific mechanism, which FAILED, and that is worth recording.** Hypothesis: Apple-Silicon E-core scheduling, which would explain a clean bimodal gap that continuous contention would not. Control: the same guard under `taskpolicy -b` (background QoS). Result: **12/12 over cap at 1.628–1.846 ms — a ~5× slowdown, not the 1.8–2.6× s1160 observed.** So **pure E-core placement is NOT the slow mode**; the real shape is a MIXTURE — some fraction of the 160 samples served slow — which also explains why p95 (`samples[151]`, the 152nd of 160) needs **≥9** degraded samples to move at all, i.e. a sustained stall, never a single blip. **(3) THE RECOMMENDATION HOLDS, WITH A LIMIT NOBODY HAD STATED:** min-of-3 over consecutive triples scored **0/4 over cap in the default arm** — it works — but **4/4 in the background-QoS arm**. **min-of-3 cures transient steal and CANNOT rescue a systematically deprioritised process**, so it must not be sold as a general cure. ➡️ **Therefore the stronger fix, and it is this repo’s own instrument-control idiom (the one that blocked E7 attempt 1): measure a fixed known-cost reference loop in the SAME process and report it.** If the reference is also degraded, the honest verdict is **“environment degraded”**, not “PowerGraph regressed” — which is the actual defect here, since the guard currently blames the code for the box. ⛔ Still do **NOT** loosen the cap. **The n=20 baseline above plus this n=12 two-arm control are jointly the gate for proving any fix.**

🔧 **F-2174-1 (s2174, 2026-08-22, MEASURED + CURED + GUARDED) — THE RETENTION AUDIT AND ITS OWN SALVAGE TOOL SHARED ONE BLIND SPOT, SO THE TOOL THAT SAVES AND THE TOOL THAT VERIFIES THE SAVE FAILED TOGETHER.** ✓ Not inferred: `art-staging-audit.mjs:136` and `salvage-art-staging.mjs:110` each carried `if (e.name.startsWith('.')) continue;`, excluding every dot-prefixed file from the scan set **BY CONSTRUCTION**. 🔧 **F-2175-1 (s2175, 2026-08-22, MEASURED + CURED + GUARDED) — THE CURED CLASS SURVIVED IN A THIRD SITE, AND THAT SITE IS THE ALARM ITSELF.** ✓ Not inferred: `scripts/health-watch.sh:75` counted the ART slot with `find worktrees/art/assets -type f -not -path '*/.*'`, which drops **every path containing a dot-prefixed segment BEFORE the blob check runs**. A third implementation of the same question — in another language, so it could never share the declaration — sat outside it. **When you cure a class in N sites, the guard's denominator must be the QUESTION, not the files you touched**; ask what else asks this, in any language. (Standing shape: an alarm is frequently a third implementation of the question a tool and its verifier already answer.) ✅ **CURE (`8acd82032`): skip VCS/OS noise BY NAME** — `.git/`, `.git`, `.DS_Store`, `.localized`, `Thumbs.db` — the same rule its two siblings carry. **Effect: scans 983 → 1019, reports 0 → 36, matching `art-staging-audit.mjs` to the file; two independent instruments now agree.** 🔒 **GUARDED, AND BOTH RED PATHS PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING THE DEFECT, NEVER BY A GREEN** (`salvage-art-staging-reach.test.mjs`, **15/15**): (1) regressing `art_untracked()` to the blanket `-not -path '*/.*'` **reds** with the F-2175-1 message; (2) widening the audit's `SKIP_NAMES` while leaving the alarm behind **reds** on drift. The new assertion reads the skip names **out of the audit's own `SKIP_NAMES` literal** rather than re-hardcoding them, so a future widening of one site cannot silently leave the alarm behind. ⚖️ **The alarm is EDGE-triggered (`AU > 0 && AU != OLDAU`), so the now-visible 36 fires once and then goes quiet — it does NOT become a permanently-screaming alert, and a 37th at-risk file will still alert.** ⓘ **Expect `art staged, in NO commit: 36` on the dashboard from now on — that is the CURE working, not a new hole**, and it is the same 36 as the audit's, not an additional set.
🔬 **F-2175-2 (s2175, 2026-08-22, VERIFIED — AN INHERITED INFERENCE UPGRADED TO PROOF, AND IT HOLDS).** F-2174-1's row above rules the 36 at-risk takes REDUNDANT on **byte-sum arithmetic over a single sampled case** (`hero-attack-down-takes123.png` 1,157,051 B vs the three takes' 1,158,199 B). That is suggestive, not containment — near-equal PNG sizes are consistent with a re-render, a downscale, or a coincidence, and **four fires had just been shown reporting a good-faith zero from an instrument nobody had re-derived**, so this claim was exactly the kind that should not be inherited (Mistake #4). **It was tested, and s2174 was right.** ✓ **METHOD, IN THREE INDEPENDENT STEPS.** (1) **Arithmetic generalised**: the ratio holds across **all 12** composites, not the one sampled — composite/sum ranges 0.9982–0.9994, consistent with one PNG header paid once instead of three times. (2) **Geometry**: decoding the IHDR of all 48 files, **every composite is 1440×540 and every take 1440×180** — an exact vertical 3-up, 12/12. (3) **Pixels**: decoding each composite to raw RGBA, slicing band *k*, and sha-256-ing it against the decoded take — **36 of 36 bands are byte-identical to their take, 0 differing.** 🔑 **AND THE PREMISE NOBODY HAD CHECKED, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT COULD HAVE COLLAPSED THE WHOLE ARGUMENT: are the COMPOSITES actually safe?** "Redundant" is worthless if the thing holding the copy dies with the same disk. Measured against **all 134 remote-tracking refs** (89,668 reachable objects): **12/12 composites are in the object database AND reachable from an origin ref.** ⇒ **VERDICT: losing all 36 files loses ZERO information.** The bytes are recoverable, pixel-exact, from blobs that already survive this disk. ➡️ **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OWNER'S PENDING DISPOSITION (F-1120-2 / F-1055-2): this ARGUES AGAINST salvaging them.** Committing 12.43 MB of provably-recoverable bytes adds weight to a git repository already under an open 5 GB advisory, for no information gain — so the correct act is to **record them as verified-redundant rather than to preserve them**, and the RETENTION LAW is not violated by declining to duplicate bytes it already holds. **No fire acted on this**; the disposition remains the owner's, but it can now be decided on proof instead of on arithmetic. 💡 **THE REUSABLE HALF: the cheap check and the true check disagreed about nothing here — but only because someone ran the true one.** A size-sum within 0.1% is the sort of evidence that is almost always right and is not therefore proof; when a standing disposition rests on it, spend the hour. **Recorded here so no future fire re-decodes 48 PNGs to re-derive a settled fact.**
🗄️ **SHOULD A SAVED PROFILE THAT PREDATES PROFILE-SCOPED STORAGE BE RESCUED, OR LEFT BEHIND? (F-1113-5, raised s1113, put on this desk s1114 — triage, not a fire.)** ✓ VERIFIED by a runner's own storage probe, quoted verbatim: *"after reload the raw epoch existed but the scoped key did not; migration did not create it."* **Nothing is broken today and nothing is waiting on you to unblock a merge** — the four fixtures that surfaced this were fixed at `5097b3e6` by seeding the key the product actually reads, so they are correct under every hypothesis. **The open question is product-side and small but real:** `migrateProfileDataKeys()` (`ProfileStorage.ts:342-350`) does **not** move an existing *raw* profile-data key to its profile-scoped name. So a player whose browser holds a pre-scoping key keeps it, while the game reads the scoped one and sees a fresh profile. **Whether that is right depends on a call only you can make:** say **"rescue"** and a fire teaches migration to adopt a raw key when no scoped key exists *(this is the player-friendly reading — an old save survives the upgrade)*; say **"leave it"** and we record that pre-scoping keys are deliberately abandoned, and no future fixture or feature is allowed to lean on migration to save them *(also defensible — it keeps one key format and avoids resurrecting stale state)*. ⛔ **A fire did not just pick one because it changes what happens to real saved player data on upgrade** (§7.3). **Cost either way: one small slice, same day.** Note the honest limit on the evidence: this was observed in a test fixture's storage, not reproduced against a real aged player profile — worth one probe before implementing whichever you choose.

But the spec **also statically imports the balance table node-side** (`:4`, `import { Balance } from '../src/game/Balance'`), and `:262`'s `waitForSim(page, Balance.wreck.repairSeconds + 0.3)` is a **node-side read**: it keeps meaning **1.2 + 0.3 simulated seconds no matter what the page is told.** The two processes hold different copies of the module; a page-side override is **invisible to node**. **Consequence:** the refresh's own scope-3 (raise `wreck.repairSeconds` to `N` per-test to widen the `:260` observation window) would leave the `:252` test waiting ~1.5 sim seconds for a repair that now needs `N` — so `:263` (no `repair_palisade` sink logged) and `:264` (still wrecked) would pass **trivially even if the repair-interrupt were completely broken.** That is the **F-1026-1 vacuous-guard class reached by accident rather than intent**, which is the worse way to reach it, because nothing about the diff looks like a weakened assertion. **Fixed in the master before it ever ran:** one local const now feeds both the `setBalance` call and the `waitForSim` argument, and **scope 4 gains a second mutation control aimed exactly at this** — remove the interrupt so the repair completes; `:263`/`:264` **must** go red; if they stay green the wait is shorter than the dwell and the guard is vacuous. **Also verified while checking:** `:262` is the **ONLY** node-side read of `Balance.wreck.repairSeconds` in the file (`grep -n "Balance\."`), so the re-key is complete at that one line; and `waitForSim` (`:84-91`) waits in **simulated** seconds against `timeAlive` with a **15s real** timeout, so even `N=8` costs ~1.04s real at `timescale=8` — the re-key cannot blow the timeout. **LESSON (the third fire in a row saved by measuring instead of inheriting, and the first where the stale claim was itself a *verification claim*): "verified at file:line" in a predecessor's handoff is still a CLAIM. It carries a timestamp and an author, not a guarantee — Mistake #4 does not exempt sentences containing the word "verified". The re-probe cost two greps.**

## s1071 (2026-07-26, fire) — THE REFILL CAME BACK GREEN IN 14 MINUTES, AND BOTH "DEFECTS" TURNED OUT TO BE THE TEST LYING ABOUT THE ENGINE
→ `tasks/backlog/s1071.md` — 2 closed row(s) moved there by `scripts/backlog-split-closed.mjs` (owner ruling 2026-09-24, item 13a); nothing was deleted.
- 🔬 **F-1068-2 SOLVED, and the deciding line is the harness's — I re-derived it from source rather than accepting the runner's conclusion, because the master demanded exactly that.** `fallbackReason = 'debug-disabled'` is set at `src/meta/ContractFamilies.ts:1148` only when `requestedId && !debug && !launched && !liveSagaFlagship`. `launched` is `isPlayerContractLaunch()` (`:1208`), which is literally **`sessionStorage.getItem(PLAYER_CONTRACT_LAUNCH_KEY) === id`** (`:1210`); the key is written by `stagePlayerContractLaunch()` (`:1078`), whose caller `launchContract()` (`src/main.ts:213-221`) stages it and then calls **`window.location.reload()`** — a real navigation. The test's `seedProfile()` installed a Playwright `addInitScript` containing **`sessionStorage.clear()`**, and `addInitScript` re-runs on *every* navigation — so it wiped the launch key **on the post-click reload, before the app booted and read it**, manufacturing `launched === false` in the test and nowhere else. Deleting that one line is the whole repair. **The sibling helper `clearStorage()` (`:143`) correctly keeps its `sessionStorage.clear()`** — its tests go straight to `/?debug&contract=…`, where `debug` short-circuits the launch-key check. Not a Mistake #10 shape after all; the player was never affected.
- 🔬 **F-1068-3 SOLVED — the engine locked the card CORRECTLY and the fixture was under-seeded.** `e1-baron`'s rule is `science-complete+2-secured` (`src/meta/ContractUnlock.ts:48-54`), requiring science complete **and** `securedContracts.size >= 2` — *two distinct secured contract ids*. The fixture seeded exactly one (`the-claim`), so `data-contract-locked="true"` was the right answer. Seeding `e1-dry-gulch` as the second makes the fixture model a player who has genuinely earned the whole E1 board — **a precondition repair, not a bent expectation**: the unlock rule is untouched and the neighbouring rungs stay coherent (`e1-dry-gulch` = `wave10OnClaim`, `e1-twin-banks` = `firstSecuredClaim`, `e1-night-shift` = `science≥3`).
- 🧾 **EVIDENCE, real numbers: tsc clean · build green (`✓ 1.30s`) · own spec `--workers=1` **14/14 passed (1.6m) — 7/7 desktop-chrome + 7/7 mobile-chrome at 390px**, exactly the 7/7-both-projects s1070 predicted · both formerly-failing tests now green (`plain no-debug board launch…` 5.1s/4.8s; `board cards show the same briefing data` 5.0s/5.4s) · console + page errors **zero**, asserted in-suite at `:299-300` inside passing tests · adjacent `board-era-chapters` + `board-gating-and-profiles` + `board-upcoming-surveys` **12/12 GREEN** both projects.**
