## s1072 (2026-07-26, fire) — THE UNOWNED ONBOARDING RED HAS A ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS A SPAWN POINT THAT MOVED TWO UNITS SEVEN DAYS AGO
- 🔬 **F-1072-1 (ROOT-CAUSED from a dry board — F-1071-2 is no longer unowned).** `061-first-claim-onboarding` has been red since **2026-07-19**, and three fires carried it as *"unowned, wants an attended triage rung."* It is now explained end to end, by measurement rather than by reading. **Reproduced first:** `--project=desktop-chrome --workers=1` ⇒ **3 failed / 1 passed**, matching the s1068/s1071 fingerprint exactly; the failure is `expect(getByTestId('town-bark-speaker')).toHaveText('Marta Vale')` at `e2e/061-first-claim-onboarding.spec.ts:74`, **Received: `"Elder Rowan"`**. The single passing test is the only one that never calls `waitForFirstClaimGuide()`.
- 🎯 **THE MECHANISM: the greeter is chosen by PROXIMITY between exactly two candidates, and the player's spawn point moved across the midpoint.** `TownScene.firstClaimGreeter()` (`src/town/TownScene.ts:1293-1307`) iterates the roster and **skips every actor except `tavernkeeper` and `elder`**, returning whichever is nearest the hero — with no bark-radius gate, so it always returns one of the two. **`5e527a28` (2026-07-19, `runner(lane-a): lane-landmark-collision.md`) changed `HERO_START` from `(0, 0.06, 0)` to `(0, 0.06, 2)`** — a two-unit shift made to fix a landmark collision, which crossed the midpoint between Marta Vale and Elder Rowan and **silently reassigned the onboarding greeting**. Distances computed both ways, and the flip is robust in both coordinate systems: at **z=0** Marta 8.64 / Rowan 9.91 ⇒ **Marta greets**; at **z=2** Marta 10.28 / Rowan 8.53 ⇒ **Rowan greets** (definition coords) — and at the plaza-placed RUNTIME coords the same flip holds (z=0: Marta 8.11 / Rowan 9.50; z=2: Marta 9.44 / Rowan 8.53).
- 🧾 **THREE CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS WERE KILLED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE SURVIVED, and each kill is worth recording.** **(1) "the town layout drifted"** — FALSE: both actors' `position` literals in `src/town/townsfolk.ts` are **byte-identical at every commit** from `c5954768` through HEAD. **(2) "the roster gating changed and the elder appeared"** — FALSE: `requiresBuilding` is **absent on both** at every one of those commits (it gates only `storekeeper`/`preacher`), so both have always been visible. **(3) "the townsfolk walk, so the winner is racy"** — FALSE: `TownActorRuntime.position` *is* live (`:2267`) and *is* time-driven for looping actors (`:2299`), but **`loop` is absent on both greeter candidates** (only `youngster_a`/`youngster_b`/`newsie`/`prospector` walk), so the selection is deterministic, not flaky.
- ⚠️ **METHOD WARNING, paid for in this fire: a `-S` pickaxe that says "never changed" is not evidence about a value that changed inside an unchanged line.** `git log -S "HERO_START = new THREE.Vector3"` reported **only** the 2026-07-07 creation and appeared to exonerate the spawn outright — because the pickaxe reports commits where the **count** of a string changes, and that literal occurs exactly once before and after. **`-G` (regex) found `5e527a28` immediately.** The false exoneration cost most of an investigation and nearly shipped "cause unknown."
- ⚖️ **WHICH SIDE IS WRONG — the ENGINE IS COHERENT AND THE ASSERTION OVER-SPECIFIES, but the flip was an ACCIDENT, and those two facts point at different fixes.** For the engine: the two-candidate whitelist is deliberate and **unchanged since the feature shipped**, and the greeting line itself — `FIRST_CLAIM_GREETING` (`:111`) = *"The valley's open. **The tavern keeps the contracts.** Go stake your first claim."* — is written in the **third person about the tavern**, which reads correctly from the schoolhouse elder and distinctly oddly from the tavernkeeper standing inside her own tavern. The guide trail still targets the tavernkeeper (`:1240`), so the chain *elder greets → trail → tavern → board → launch* is coherent. Against: `5e527a28` was a **landmark-collision fix** with no stated intent to touch onboarding, so today's greeter is **accidental, not designed** — and relaxing the test would bless an accident. **The spec has been modified exactly once, at its introduction, so the assertion is original and was correct on the day it was written.**
- 🛑 **NO CORRECTIVE AUTHORED, and the reason is §7.3 rather than §2E's hard limit.** Both repairs are one-liners and neither is a fire's call: **(a)** relax `:74` to accept either whitelisted greeter — matches the engine's ratified contract, but ratifies a side effect; **(b)** pin `firstClaimGreeter()` to `tavernkeeper` (or nudge `HERO_START` back), restoring the greeter the feature shipped with. **This is a design fork about who welcomes a brand-new player on the E1 release path, so it goes to the desk with a recommendation instead of into a lane.** Zero console/page errors throughout: nothing is crashing, it is a question of whose voice the onboarding speaks in.
- 🧾 **EVIDENCE:** probe `logs/_s1072_greeter_probe.mjs` (retained per the RETENTION LAW) reproduces the spec's seed + naming ceremony and reads the live values: rendered speaker **`"Elder Rowan"`**, `activeBark.actorId` **`elder`**, `firstClaimGuide` `{active:true, greetingVisible:true, trailVisible:true}`, **console/page errors 0**. Its first draft failed on **guessed** localStorage keys; the real ones were then read from `src/game/ProfileStorage.ts` (`PROFILE_KEY = 'gr.profile.v2'`, `profileDataKey = PROFILE_KEY + '.' + id + '.' + logicalKey`) rather than guessed a second time.
- 📉 **DEPLOY STALENESS REFRESHED BY ASKING THE LIVE SITE, not inherited: `https://gold-rush-3in.pages.dev/version.json` still returns `{"build":"9fa96680","builtAt":"2026-07-24T17:20:23Z"}`, and `git rev-list --count 9fa96680..main` is now **296 commits behind**, up from the 220 s1057 recorded.** `logs/deploy-result.json` still reads `deploy_failed` (`0c82ce4c`, 2026-07-26T00:01Z). Unchanged in cause, still owner-gated on F-1051-3 option (2).
- 🧾 **DUTIES: NO drain** (board verified fully dry on entry — 0 queued across all six slots, 0 running, 0 undrained done-moves; the three newest `tasks/done/` entries all map to merges `5f399dd6` / `79de56f4` / `f8812586`) · **NO refill and NO master authored** (b/c/d/art/main on named owner gates; lane-a's next rung still blocked behind F-1069-2 + F-1070-1) · **NO gazette** (zero player-visible bytes merged) · **NO deploy** (zero gameplay bytes) · **no `goals.json` leaf** (the Law binds authoring and draining; this fire did neither) · **ticker: Jul-25 paid (`a417807d (archive: pruned by the A3 rewrite)`); `ticker-digest-2026-07-26.md` due TOMORROW ≥06:00 local**, covering `79de56f4` + `f8812586` + `5f399dd6` · **assayer `pending/` empty · no `CODEX-WALL` · no ART slot touched**, so the art-audit law did not bind · **liveness re-measured, not inherited:** two TTY-resident `claude` pids (`67079`, `8567`) both near-idle (`8567`: 3:35 CPU over 10h57m, last attended commit 08:21), accounts-playwright `24384` still **8 days elapsed / 0:00.54 CPU** and the `:8788`/`:8799` wranglers still 16-day zombies, **no live `codex exec`** ⇒ the runner was idle and the log churn was mine to take.

🔴 **F-1081-10 — THE DEPLOY FAILURE IS A REPRODUCIBLE *TRANSPORT* FAILURE, NOT AUTH AND NOT SIZE. THE STANDING DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, AND THIS NOW BLOCKS SIX MERGED GAMEPLAY CHANGES.** ✓ VERIFIED s1081 by running `bash scripts/deploy.sh` **twice** and reading the wrangler log both times — the first fresh attempt since s1078, because re-running a known-failing command is only pointless if you don't read the log. Both attempts fail identically at `pages deploy`, exit 0 (the script never blocks, as designed), with `✘ Failed to upload files. Please try again. Error: {}` — an **empty** error object, which is why this has been mis-attributed. The log tells the real story: repeated `TypeError: fetch failed` whose `[cause]` is **`Error: write EPIPE`** and **`SocketError: other side closed`**, across many parallel upload connections, fatal after ~30 s.

**What this rules OUT, with evidence:**
- **NOT auth** — zero `401`/`403`/`token`/`scope` anywhere in the log; wrangler authenticates and reaches the API fine.
- **NOT quota/rate** — no `429`.
- **NOT the ~118 MB size theory** (s1078's premise): the script's own budget check **passes with room to spare** — `16,480,199 bytes` against the cap, **8,519,801 bytes of headroom**, on both desktop and mobile.
- **NOT a one-off transient** — the retry reproduced it exactly, so "Please try again" is not the answer either. (And bandwidth is not the constraint: F-1076-1 measured a **184.9 MB** git push completing in **65 s** on this machine.)

**What it points AT:** the connection is being closed mid-write by the far side, repeatedly, under wrangler's *parallel* upload fan-out. Candidate causes worth one owner-side look each: wrangler 4.107.0's upload concurrency against this network path (a proxy, a router, or an ISP dropping many simultaneous long-lived POSTs), or a Cloudflare-side per-connection limit. ➡️ **CHEAP THINGS TO TRY BEFORE ANY BIG DECISION:** (a) a concurrency/`--no-bundle`-style throttle on the Pages upload, (b) the same deploy from a different network, (c) a wrangler version change. **`scripts/deploy.sh` also has no retry and no upload-concurrency control at all** — adding both is small, fire-authorable, and testable only by an owner-present run.
⚠️ **This supersedes the framing of F-1051-3 "option (2)".** The owner may have been offered the wrong choice: the blocker looks like a fixable transport setting, not something requiring the option-(2) tradeoff. **Six merged gameplay changes are now unplayable by the family** (`4154da9e`, `e886150a`, `50acfeff`, `2dfa0b4d`, `6f6345c1`, and today's `1dbd0120` + `33aac820`), which makes this the highest-value owner item on the desk.

- 🔴 **BUT THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT — "so no release suite gates a deploy", implying the fix is to wire it in — IS FALSE AND ACTIVELY DANGEROUS. `test:release` validates a DIFFERENT BUILD than the one deployed.** `scripts/deploy.sh:49` publishes `npm run build` = **all-epoch**. `test:release` (`playwright.release.config.ts`) validates `GR_RELEASE=e1 npm run build:release` = **E1-only**, and its assertions demand the *absence* of later content: `e2e/release-build.spec.ts:165` asserts `e7-relay-valley`/`e10-last-claim` **decline to the Claim**, and `:195` asserts dist has **no later manifest ids or plate/GLB assets**.

Current `dist/` is genuinely the deployed shape: **406 GLBs**, later-epoch ids present. So the suite is not merely unwired — **it is incompatible with the deploy by construction.**

Its 0 refs are CORRECT** — it is an option-measuring instrument for an un-taken owner decision, not an orphaned guard. Standing operational trap worth knowing: **any fire that runs `npm run test:release` leaves `dist/` E1-only** (s1056 hit this and restored it by hand); `deploy.sh` self-protects only because it rebuilds at `:49` first.

Zero behavioural assertions can stop a bad build reaching the family.**

## s1455 (2026-08-04, fire) — A HOLD VERDICT HAS NO ENFORCEMENT SURFACE, AND NOW IT HAS A GUARD

- 🛠️ **F-1455-1 — THE STALE-HOLD-VERDICT CLASS IS MECHANIZED: `scripts/stale-hold-verdict-guard.test.mjs`, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (12 guards now — COUNT it, never prune it).** s1454 found the class by hand — a review whose `## VERDICT` still refuses the merge while its goal leaf says the slice shipped — bannered three rows and *recommended* a guard rather than building one at fire-end (F-1300-4: a fire mutates gate topology late and then cannot see it). This fire had a drain-dry board and built it at fire START, with the full battery as the last act. ⚖️ **The class is real and it is BIGGER than the hand sweep found: s1455 re-derived it independently and caught TWO MORE that a sample of nine had missed.** (1) `reviews/gg-03-gazette-panel-swap.md` said **⛔ BLOCKED — do not merge** while the panel swap has been live on main since 2026-07-29 — `src/news/heraldReader.ts:177` carries the exact `<img class="claim-herald__art-slot" data-testid="gazette-panel-engraving">` it describes, discharged by the GG-03c ladder at `15e00755`. ⚠️ **That commit is headlined** *"fix: goals.json schema — two violations turned test:node-guards red on main (F-1211-2)"* **and in fact carries six `gazette-panel-*.webp` plates plus the herald engravings — a headline names intent, `--stat` names content.** (2) `reviews/m2-05-geometry-settle.md` said **"The leaf does NOT close"**; the leaf closed at `94ce3888` *"s1040: drain m2-05-geometry-settle — F-1035-1 geometry race CLOSED by a stability wait, proved twice over"*, **fifteen fires earlier**, verified by ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 94ce3888 main` rc=0) and never by the leaf status field. Its done-move sits in `tasks/failed/` as `shipped-s1064-99bd76fd.md` — a `shipped-` prefix inside `failed/`, the shape that makes this class invisible to a directory-level sweep. Both now carry supersede banners with the original verdicts KEPT verbatim (retention law).
- ⚠️ **AND THE REUSABLE HALF IS THAT THE CLASSIFIER, NOT THE LOOKUP, IS THE HARD PART — MY OWN FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE LESSON WARNS (a fresh classifier's first hits are probably its own bug).** Matching `HOLD|HELD|NOT MERGED|WITHHELD|BLOCKED` anywhere in the verdict LINE produced six hits of which **four were the instrument, not the board**: `e2-rail-tough-only-bind` (*"MERGE — the firewall **held** byte-for-byte"*), `f1420-1` (*"MERGE — gates green, scope 4's STOP condition **held**"*), `eight-winds-e2-row-order-survey` (*"**ACCEPTED** — the wiring slice stays **blocked**"*) and `art-e7-town-icons` (*"QA PASS — reference-tier, extraction **WITHHELD**"*). Every one is a MERGE verdict whose prose happens to discuss holding — **which is what review prose is about.** A guard reddening on those trains fires to ignore it, which is worse than no guard. ➡️ **The guard therefore classifies on the DECISION TOKEN ONLY** — the span before the first em-dash, period or comma — and all four false positives are pinned as fixtures so the sentence form cannot creep back. ⓘ **Lookup needed three keys, also measured rather than assumed:** of 13 mappable refusals, **6 resolved by file stem, 4 by `taskFile`, 3 by the Slice header**. `gg-03` is the instructive one — **its leaf id names the BLOCKED slice while its `taskFile` names the SUCCESSOR that discharged it**, so a `taskFile`-only lookup would never have found the stale row it was built to find.
- ✅ **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING THE DEFECT, NOT BY A GREEN (the s1299/s1300 standard) — a passing guard never executes its violation path.** `artifacts/s1455/manufacture-defect.mjs` copies the full 683-file reviews corpus to `/tmp` (**never into main's working tree — §3.0b custody, and two lanes were live**), strips one supersede banner, and runs the guard against it: **rc=1 both times**, naming exactly one offender each time, with the corpus-size assertions still GREEN — so the red is attributable to the manufactured defect rather than to a shrunken corpus. Both banners are therefore proven **load-bearing**. ⓘ The guard's paths are env-redirectable **only** so this probe can run outside main's tree; the redirect **cannot silence it** — the instrument-validation test asserts a large corpus, so pointing it anywhere small REDS rather than greens. **Unmapped refusals (4) are REPORTED, never red**: an unmatched review is F-1448-6 leaf debt, a different finding with a different owner. **GATE: closed — the guard is rooted, its red path is proven, and the two stale rows it found are bannered.**
